atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: Always.
atoms.effect: Chapter 12 applies in every Virginia jurisdiction; no locality, board, or court may waive or modify it.
atoms.quote: This chapter shall apply to all jurisdictions in the Commonwealth and may not be waived or otherwise modified, in whole or in part, by the governing body of any locality or its boards or commissions or other instrumentalities or by the courts of the Commonwealth.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.actor: landlord of public housing or other HUD-regulated dwelling unit
atoms.condition: Occupancy is in a public housing unit or other housing unit that is a dwelling unit, and a chapter 12 provision is inconsistent with HUD regulations.
atoms.effect: The chapter applies to such occupancy, but HUD regulations control where inconsistent with it.
judgment_terms: inconsistent (whether a HUD rule conflicts with a chapter 12 rule)
atoms.quote: Occupancy in a public housing unit or other housing unit that is a dwelling unit is subject to this chapter; however, if the provisions of this chapter are inconsistent with the regulations of the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, such regulations shall control.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: Occupancy of a single-family or multifamily dwelling unit in Virginia.
atoms.effect: The chapter applies to every single-family and multifamily dwelling unit. The current text has no exemption or opt-in for small or natural-person landlords; unit-count thresholds exist only inside particular subsections (55.1-1204(J)(2), (K); 55.1-1245 payment-plan and COVID subsections; 55.1-1250(A); 55.1-1209(F) from 2027-07-01).
atoms.quote: The provisions of this chapter shall apply to occupancy in all single-family and multifamily dwelling units and multifamily dwelling units located in the Commonwealth.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The occupancy is one of: institutional residence incidental to detention or medical, geriatric, educational, counseling, religious or similar services; fraternal/social organization member; condominium owner or cooperative proprietary lessee; campground; tenant who pays no rent; employee whose multifamily occupancy is conditioned on employment (or former employee for under 60 days); purchaser under contract of sale; recovery residence.
atoms.effect: The occupancy is not a residential tenancy under chapter 12, so the chapter 12 settlement rules (55.1-1226 etc.) do not govern it.
judgment_terms: incidental to detention or the provision of medical, geriatric, educational, counseling, religious, or similar services
conditioned upon employment in and about the premises
atoms.quote: The following tenancies and occupancies are not residential tenancies under this chapter:

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The occupant pays no rent under a rental agreement.
atoms.effect: Not a residential tenancy under the chapter.
atoms.quote: Occupancy by a tenant who pays no rent pursuant to a rental agreement;

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: Occupant is an employee whose right to occupy a multifamily unit is conditioned on employment in and about the premises, or a former employee whose occupancy continues less than 60 days.
atoms.effect: Not a residential tenancy under the chapter.
judgment_terms: conditioned upon employment in and about the premises
atoms.quote: Occupancy by an employee of a landlord whose right to occupancy in a multifamily dwelling unit is conditioned upon employment in and about the premises or a former employee whose occupancy continues less than 60 days;

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.actor: owner of hotel, motel, extended stay, vacation or similar transient lodging
atoms.condition: A person resides in such lodging as primary residence for 90 consecutive days or less.
atoms.effect: The lodging is not subject to chapter 12 (five-day nonpayment notice and self-help eviction apply instead).
atoms.quote: If a person resides in a hotel, motel, extended stay facility, vacation residential facility, including those governed by the Virginia Real Estate Time-Share Act (§ 55.1-2200 et seq.), boardinghouse, or similar transient lodging as his primary residence for 90 consecutive days or less, such lodging shall not be subject to the provisions of this chapter.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: A person resides in transient lodging as primary residence for more than 90 consecutive days, or is subject to a written lease for more than 90 days.
atoms.effect: The lodging is subject to chapter 12, including its deposit and settlement rules.
atoms.quote: If a person resides in a hotel, motel, extended stay facility, vacation residential facility, including those governed by the Virginia Real Estate Time-Share Act (§ 55.1-2200 et seq.), boardinghouse, or similar transient lodging as his primary residence for more than 90 consecutive days or is subject to a written lease for more than 90 days, such lodging shall be subject to the provisions of this chapter.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: Always.
atoms.effect: Chapter 12 supersedes all other local ordinances and regulations on landlord-tenant relations and residential leasing. Virginia has no local layer for this chain (localities keep only reconciliatory mediation commissions and property-maintenance-code ordinances).
atoms.quote: This chapter shall supersede all other local ordinances or regulations concerning landlord and tenant relations and the leasing of residential property.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: Tenancy is nonresidential.
atoms.effect: Chapter 14 of Title 55.1 governs nonresidential tenancies; residential tenancies are governed by chapter 12, so chapter 14 is not a parallel residential regime.
atoms.quote: The provisions of this chapter shall apply to all nonresidential tenancies.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 59.1
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The aspect of the consumer transaction is subject to the VRLTA.
atoms.effect: The Virginia Consumer Protection Act does not apply, unless the landlord's act or practice is a misrepresentation or fraudulent act or practice under 59.1-200 (which then exposes the landlord to VCPA remedies).
atoms.quote: Any aspect of a consumer transaction that is subject to the Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act (§ 55.1-1200 et seq.) or Chapter 14 (§ 55.1-1400 et seq.) of Title 55.1, unless the act or practice of a landlord constitutes a misrepresentation or fraudulent act or practice under § 59.1-200.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 59.1
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The actor is a real estate licensee under Title 54.1 ch. 21.
atoms.effect: The VCPA does not apply to the licensee unless the act is a violation of the Unfair Real Estate Service Agreement Act.
atoms.quote: Real estate licensees who are licensed under Chapter 21 (§ 54.1-2100 et seq.) of Title 54.1, unless the act or practice of the licensee constitutes a violation of law under the Unfair Real Estate Service Agreement Act (§ 55.1-3200 et seq.).

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: Drafting or enforcing a rental agreement.
atoms.effect: A lease may not make the tenant waive or forgo rights or remedies under chapter 12 (including the deposit rules).
atoms.quote: Agrees to waive or forgo rights or remedies under this chapter;

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: A lease term makes the tenant pay the landlord's attorney fees.
atoms.effect: Such a term is prohibited except as chapter 12 itself provides (e.g., 55.1-1245(H), 55.1-1251, 55.1-1253(C), 55.1-1233).
atoms.quote: Agrees to pay the landlord's attorney fees except as provided in this chapter;

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: Before commencement, the tenant pays a security deposit plus damage-insurance and renter's-insurance premiums.
atoms.effect: The total may not exceed two months' periodic rent; a lease term agreeing to more is prohibited.
atoms.quote: Agrees to the payment of a security deposit, insurance premiums for damage insurance, and insurance premiums for renter's insurance prior to the commencement of the tenancy that exceed the amount of two months' periodic rent; or

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: A rental agreement contains a provision prohibited by 55.1-1208(A).
atoms.effect: The provision is unenforceable; if the landlord sues to enforce it, the tenant may recover actual damages and reasonable attorney fees.
atoms.quote: Any provision prohibited by subsection A that is included in a rental agreement is unenforceable. If a landlord brings an action to enforce any such provision, the tenant may recover actual damages sustained by him and reasonable attorney fees.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: A fee for maintenance or repair of the dwelling unit is charged.
atoms.effect: No landlord may require a tenant to pay a maintenance or repair fee unless the repair is necessitated by the tenant's violation of a chapter 12 requirement. Limits what may be charged at move-out as "other charges".
atoms.quote: Unless necessitated by the tenant's violation of a requirement of this chapter, no landlord shall require a tenant to pay any fee for the maintenance or repair of any dwelling unit.
atoms.version_note: Text as amended by Acts 2026 c. 722/723 (clean enacted text at sources/VA_Acts2026_c722.txt; c. 723 verified identical, sources/VA_Acts2026_c723.txt; c. 722 has no delayed-effective clause); history line: 1974, c. 680, § 55-248.9; 1977, c. 427; 1987, c. 473; 1991, c. 720; 2000, c. 760; 2002, c. 531; 2003, c. 905; 2016, c. 744; 2019, c. 712; 2020, c. 998; 2021, Sp. Sess. I, cc. 427, 477, 478; 2025, cc. 684, 688; 2026, cc. 722, 723.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: Any money owed or paid under the rental agreement other than a security deposit.
atoms.effect: That money is rent (so it can be applied under 55.1-1226(A)(i) and is subject to rent remedies).
atoms.quote: "Rent" means all money, other than a security deposit, owed or paid to the landlord under the rental agreement, including prepaid rent paid more than one month in advance of the rent due date.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: Refundable money furnished by the tenant to secure lease performance, as security for damages, or as a pet deposit.
atoms.effect: It is a security deposit governed by 55.1-1226; before the commencement date it is an application deposit; a damage or renter's insurance policy bought by the landlord for the tenant is not a security deposit.
atoms.quote: "Security deposit" means any refundable deposit of money that is furnished by a tenant to a landlord to secure the performance of the terms and conditions of a rental agreement, as a security for damages to the leased premises, or as a pet deposit. However, such money shall be deemed an application deposit until the commencement date of the rental agreement.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: A bond or commercial insurance specified in the lease that secures tenant performance and replaces all or part of a deposit.
atoms.effect: It is damage insurance (55.1-1206, 55.1-1226(I)-(J)), not a security deposit.
atoms.quote: "Damage insurance" means a bond or commercial insurance coverage as specified in the rental agreement to secure the performance by the tenant of the terms and conditions of the rental agreement and to replace all or part of a security deposit.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: A person entitled only under the rental agreement to occupy the unit to the exclusion of others.
atoms.effect: Is a tenant (payee on the deposit disposition). Authorized occupants, guests and non-occupying guarantors or cosigners are not tenants.
atoms.quote: "Tenant" does not include (i) an authorized occupant, (ii) a guest or invitee, or (iii) any person who guarantees or cosigns the payment of the financial obligations of a rental agreement but has no right to occupy a dwelling unit.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: A person occupying with landlord consent who has not signed the rental agreement.
atoms.effect: Has no financial obligations as a tenant, so is not a debtor for the balance and not a payee on the deposit disposition.
atoms.quote: "Authorized occupant" means a person entitled to occupy a dwelling unit with the consent of the landlord, but who has not signed the rental agreement and therefore does not have the financial obligations as a tenant under the rental agreement.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: A managing agent fails to disclose the name of the owner, lessor or sublessor.
atoms.effect: The managing agent is itself a "landlord" under chapter 12 (and so directly bears landlord duties such as 55.1-1226).
atoms.quote: "Landlord" also includes a managing agent of the premises who fails to disclose the name of such owner, lessor, or sublessor.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: A person is authorized by the landlord to act as property manager under a written property management agreement.
atoms.effect: That person is the "managing agent" (relevant to 55.1-1202 delegation, 55.1-1213, 55.1-1224, 55.1-1257).
atoms.quote: "Managing agent" means the person authorized by the landlord to act as the property manager on behalf of the landlord pursuant to the written property management agreement.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: A chapter 12 provision requires "notice".
atoms.effect: Notice is written, sent by regular mail or hand delivery, and the sender keeps proof in the form of a certificate of service it prepares confirming the mailing.
atoms.quote: "Notice" means notice given in writing by either regular mail or hand delivery, with the sender retaining sufficient proof of having given such notice in the form of a certificate of service confirming such mailing prepared by the sender.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: A person has actual knowledge of a fact, received verbal notice, or has reason to know it from the facts and circumstances.
atoms.effect: The person is deemed to have notice of the fact.
atoms.quote: However, a person shall be deemed to have notice of a fact if he has actual knowledge of it, he has received a verbal notice of it, or, from all of the facts and circumstances known to him at the time in question, he has reason to know it exists.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: A person takes steps reasonably calculated to inform another.
atoms.effect: The person has "given" notice whether or not the recipient actually learns of it (so a deadline to give notice is met by sending, not by receipt, where the provision says "give").
atoms.quote: A person "notifies" or "gives" a notice or notification to another by taking steps reasonably calculated to inform another person, whether or not the other person actually comes to know of it.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: Notice was given other than in writing.
atoms.effect: The sender bears the burden of proving the notice was given.
atoms.quote: If notice is given that is not in writing, the person giving the notice has the burden of proof to show that the notice was given to the recipient of the notice.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: A provision requires "written notice".
atoms.effect: Written notice is notice given under 55.1-1202, on paper or in retrievable electronic form, with or without an electronic signature.
atoms.quote: "Written notice" means notice given in accordance with § 55.1-1202, including any representation of words, letters, symbols, numbers, or figures, whether (i) printed in or inscribed on a tangible medium or (ii) stored in an electronic form or any other medium, retrievable in a perceivable form, and regardless of whether an electronic signature authorized by the Uniform Electronic Transactions Act (§ 59.1-479 et seq.) is affixed.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: Terms of use and occupancy of a unit.
atoms.effect: The "rental agreement" includes written and oral agreements and valid rules adopted under 55.1-1228 (the source of "other damages or charges as provided in the rental agreement").
atoms.quote: "Rental agreement" or "lease agreement" means all rental agreements, written or oral, and valid rules and regulations adopted under § 55.1-1228 embodying the terms and conditions concerning the use and occupancy of a dwelling unit and premises.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.provision: 55.1-1200 "Processing fee for payment of rent with bad check"
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: Rent was paid by a check refused for no account or insufficient funds.
atoms.effect: The processing fee the landlord may assess is the one specified in the rental agreement and may not exceed $50.
atoms.quote: "Processing fee for payment of rent with bad check" means the processing fee specified in the rental agreement, not to exceed $50, assessed by a landlord against a tenant for payment of rent with a check drawn by the tenant on which payment has been refused by the payor bank because the drawer had no account or insufficient funds.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: A provision turns on good faith.
atoms.effect: Good faith means honesty in fact in the transaction.
atoms.quote: "Good faith" means honesty in fact in the conduct of the transaction concerned.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: A person holds all or part of legal title, or beneficial ownership with a present right of use (including a mortgagee in possession).
atoms.effect: That person is an "owner" (relevant to successor-landlord and disclosure provisions).
atoms.quote: "Owner" means one or more persons or entities, jointly or severally, including a mortgagee in possession, in whom is vested:

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: A service is electricity, natural gas, or water and sewer from a public service corporation or permitted provider.
atoms.effect: It is a "utility"; if the lease so provides, submetering, energy allocation or ratio utility billing may be used.
atoms.quote: "Utility" means electricity, natural gas, or water and sewer provided by a public service corporation or such other person providing utility services as permitted under § 56-1.2.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28; same text in the version effective 2027-07-01
atoms.condition: The rental agreement provides for electronic notices.
atoms.effect: Landlord and tenant may send notices electronically.
atoms.quote: If the rental agreement so provides, the landlord and tenant may send notices in electronic form; however, any tenant who so requests may elect to send and receive notices in paper form.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28; same text from 2027-07-01
atoms.condition: A tenant requests paper notices.
atoms.effect: Notices to and from that tenant must be on paper even if the lease allows electronic notice.
atoms.quote: however, any tenant who so requests may elect to send and receive notices in paper form.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28; same text from 2027-07-01
atoms.condition: Electronic delivery is used.
atoms.effect: The sender must keep sufficient proof of electronic delivery (electronic delivery receipt, fax confirmation, or a certificate of service confirming the electronic delivery).
atoms.quote: If electronic delivery is used, the sender shall retain sufficient proof of the electronic delivery, which may be an electronic receipt of delivery, a confirmation that the notice was sent by facsimile, or a certificate of service prepared by the sender confirming the electronic delivery.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28; same text from 2027-07-01
atoms.condition: Notice is served on a landlord or on a tenant.
atoms.effect: A landlord is served at its place of business where the lease was made or any place it holds out for receipt; a tenant is served at the tenant's last known place of residence, which may be the dwelling unit (so after move-out, a forwarding address if known, else the unit).
atoms.quote: In the case of the tenant, notice is served at the tenant's last known place of residence, which may be the dwelling unit.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28; same text from 2027-07-01
atoms.condition: Notice is received by an organization.
atoms.effect: It is effective for a transaction when brought to the attention of the person conducting that transaction, or when it would have been with reasonable diligence.
atoms.quote: Notice, knowledge, or a notice or notification received by an organization is effective for a particular transaction from the time it is brought to the attention of the person conducting that transaction, or from the time it would have been brought to his attention if the organization had exercised reasonable diligence.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28; same text from 2027-07-01
atoms.condition: A private landlord serves a notice of termination on a tenant receiving tenant-based rental assistance (Housing Choice Voucher or other program).
atoms.effect: The termination notice is not effective unless its first page carries the statewide legal aid telephone number and website in type no smaller than the body.
atoms.quote: No notice of termination of tenancy served upon a tenant receiving tenant-based rental assistance through (i) the Housing Choice Voucher Program, 42 U.S.C. § 1437f(o), or (ii) any other federal, state, or local program by a private landlord shall be effective unless it contains on its first page, in type no smaller or less legible than that otherwise used in the body of the notice, the statewide legal aid telephone number and website address.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 as subsection E; re-lettered F from 2027-07-01 with same text
atoms.actor: landlord; managing agent or other third party
atoms.condition: The landlord has a written agreement delegating notice responsibility.
atoms.effect: A managing agent or other third party (e.g., Handoff) may provide any written notice under chapter 12, including the 55.1-1226 disposition; an attorney may prepare or provide notices; electronic signatures and notarizations may be used.
atoms.quote: The landlord may, in accordance with a written agreement, delegate to a managing agent or other third party the responsibility of providing any written notice under this chapter.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.condition: On or after 2027-07-01, the landlord serves a notice of termination for nonpayment of rent.
atoms.effect: The notice is ineffective unless it contains a written statement of charges and payments over the tenancy or the past 12 months (whichever is shorter), plus any contracted late charges, attorney fees, costs, other charges or damages due; with submetering/RUBS it must also list utility debits and credits and 55.1-1212(C)-(D) charges.
atoms.quote: No notice of termination of tenancy for nonpayment of rent shall be effective unless such notice contains a written statement of charges and payments over the course of the tenancy or the past 12 months, whichever is shorter, and any late charges, attorney fees, costs, and other charges or damages as contracted for in the rental agreement that are due and owing.

atoms.instrument: Acts of Assembly 2026, chapter 783
atoms.provision: Acts 2026 c. 783 (HB 1361), enactment clause 2 (identical c. 784, SB 294)
atoms.effective_from: 2026-04-13 (approved)
atoms.condition: Always.
atoms.effect: The 2026 amendments to 55.1-1202 (new subsection E), 55.1-1212 and 8.01-126 take effect 2027-07-01. The act contains no clause on leases signed before that date.
atoms.quote: 2. That the provisions of this act shall become effective on July 1, 2027.
atoms.version_note: Chapters 783 and 784 are identical apart from the chapter and bill labels (verified on the clean enacted texts, sources/VA_Acts2026_c784.txt). Quote re-checked against the clean enacted text.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The tenant has designated a third party to receive duplicate copies of written notices relating to the tenancy.
atoms.effect: The landlord must mail the duplicate to the designee at the same time the notice goes to the tenant; failure does not affect the validity of any judgment against the tenant.
atoms.quote: Where such a third party has been designated by the tenant, the landlord shall mail the duplicate copy of any summons issued pursuant to § 8.01-126 or notice to the designated third party at the same time the summons or notice is mailed to or served upon the tenant.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.actor: landlord or person authorized to lease
atoms.condition: At or before the start of the tenancy.
atoms.effect: Disclose in writing the name and address of the manager and of an owner or owner's agent, for service of process and notices.
atoms.quote: For the purpose of service of process and receiving and issuing receipts for notices and demands, the landlord or any person authorized to enter into a rental agreement on his behalf shall disclose to the tenant in writing at or before the beginning of the tenancy the name and address of:

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The premises are sold.
atoms.effect: Notify the tenant of the sale and give the purchaser's name, address and telephone number.
atoms.quote: In the event of the sale of the premises, the landlord shall notify the tenant of such sale and disclose to the tenant the name and address of the purchaser and a telephone number at which such purchaser can be located.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The disclosures are not kept current or not made.
atoms.effect: The duties bind successors; a person who fails to comply becomes an agent of each landlord for service of process and notices.
atoms.quote: The information required to be furnished by this section shall be kept current, and the provisions of this section extend to and are enforceable against any successor landlord or owner. A person who fails to comply with this section becomes an agent of each person who is a landlord for the purposes of service of process and receiving and issuing receipts for notices and demands.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: An individual owner who leases residential property does not reside in Virginia.
atoms.effect: Must appoint and keep a Virginia agent, designated in every lease, for service of process and notices.
atoms.quote: Every nonresident property owner shall appoint and continuously maintain an agent who (i) if such agent is an individual, is a resident of the Commonwealth, or if such agent is a corporation, limited liability company, partnership, or other entity, is authorized to transact business in the Commonwealth and (ii) maintains a business office within the Commonwealth.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The required agent designation has not been filed.
atoms.effect: The owner may not maintain an action in Virginia courts concerning the property (blocks suing a former tenant for a balance until filed).
atoms.quote: No nonresident property owner shall maintain an action in the courts of the Commonwealth concerning property for which a designation is required by this section until such designation has been filed.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The landlord asks the sheriff to deliver a notice under 55.1-1245 or 55.1-1415.
atoms.effect: The sheriff may deliver it for a fee of not more than $12 (this caps the service cost recoverable under 55.1-1251).
atoms.quote: For this service, the sheriff shall be allowed a fee not to exceed $12.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 1
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.actor: any actor with a statutory deadline
atoms.condition: An act must be performed within a prescribed time after an event.
atoms.effect: The day of the event is not counted.
atoms.quote: When an act of the General Assembly or rule of court requires that an act be performed within a prescribed amount of time after any event or judgment, the day on which the event or judgment occurred shall not be counted against the time allowed.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 1
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.actor: any actor with a statutory deadline
atoms.condition: A statute requires by a prescribed period that an act be performed, and the last day falls on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday (or a day the relevant government office is closed).
atoms.effect: The act may be performed on the next business day that is not a Saturday, Sunday, legal holiday or closure day. This reaches a private party's statutory deadline, including the 55.1-1226 deadlines (VA:1-210(E)-private-deadlines).
atoms.quote: When an act of the General Assembly or local governing body, order of the court, or administrative regulation or order requires, either by specification of a date or by a prescribed period of time, that an act be performed or an action be filed on a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday or on any day or part of a day on which the state or local government office where the act to be performed or the action to be filed is closed, the act may be performed or the action may be filed on the next business day that is not a Saturday, Sunday, legal holiday, or day on which the state or local government office is closed.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 1
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: A statutory limitation period for bringing an action ends on a Saturday, Sunday, legal holiday or clerk-office closure day.
atoms.effect: The action may be brought on the next day that is none of those.
atoms.quote: When an act of the General Assembly specifies a maximum period of time in which a legal action may be brought and the last day of that period falls on a Saturday, Sunday, legal holiday, or day or part of a day on which the clerk's office is closed as authorized by an act of the General Assembly, the action may be brought on the next day that is not a Saturday, Sunday, legal holiday, or day or part of a day on which the clerk's office is closed as authorized by an act of the General Assembly.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 1
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The Governor authorizes closing state government on a day.
atoms.effect: That day is a legal holiday for 1-210.
atoms.quote: For the purposes of this section, any day on which the Governor authorizes the closing of the state government shall be considered a legal holiday.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 2.2
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: Determining whether a day is a Virginia legal holiday.
atoms.effect: Legal holidays are the listed days (New Year's, MLK, George Washington Day, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, July 4, Labor Day, Columbus/Yorktown Victory Day, Election Day, Veterans Day, Thanksgiving and the Friday after, Christmas); a holiday on Saturday is observed the preceding Friday and on Sunday the following Monday; any day appointed by the Governor or the President is also a legal holiday. The calendar itself is a Stage D input.
atoms.quote: Whenever any of such days falls on Saturday, the Friday next preceding such day, or whenever any of such days falls on Sunday, the Monday next following such day, and any day so appointed by the Governor of the Commonwealth or the President of the United States, shall be a legal holiday as to the transaction of all business.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 1
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: A new act takes effect while a tenancy or claim is running.
atoms.effect: The new act does not affect any right accrued or claim arising under the former law before it takes effect; later proceedings conform, so far as practicable, to the law in force at the time of the proceedings.
atoms.quote: No new act of the General Assembly shall be construed to repeal a former law, as to any offense committed against the former law, or as to any act done, any penalty, forfeiture, or punishment incurred, or any right accrued, or claim arising under the former law, or in any way whatever to affect any such offense or act so committed or done, or any penalty, forfeiture, or punishment so incurred, or any right accrued, or claim arising before the new act of the General Assembly takes effect;

atoms.instrument: Acts of Assembly 2014, chapter 651
atoms.effective_from: 2015-01-01 (no-interest rule); approved 2014
atoms.condition: A security deposit held under the VRLTA.
atoms.effect: From 2015-01-01 no interest is due on security deposits. Interest that had accrued and was payable as of 2014-12-31 must be paid to the tenant no later than 45 days after termination and delivery of possession. Current chapter 12 contains no interest duty.
atoms.cross_time: Reaches back to deposits held before 2015; applies at termination of any tenancy that still carries pre-2015 accrued interest.
atoms.quote: That on or after January 1, 2015, there shall be no interest due and payable on security deposits of a tenant held under the Virginia Residential Landlord Tenant Act (§ 55-248.2 et seq.) of the Code of Virginia (the Act). Any accrued interest due and payable as of December 31, 2014, on security deposits of a tenant held under the Act shall be paid to such tenant no later than 45 days after termination of tenancy and delivery of possession as otherwise provided in § 55-248.15:1 of the Code of Virginia.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: A tenant takes occupancy.
atoms.effect: Within five days after occupancy, give the tenant a written report itemizing damage existing at move-in.
atoms.cross_time: Move-in baseline: evidence against which move-out damage (55.1-1226(A)(ii)) is measured.
atoms.quote: The landlord shall, within five days after occupancy of a dwelling unit, submit a written report to the tenant itemizing damages to the dwelling unit existing at the time of occupancy,

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The tenant does not object in writing within five days after receiving the report.
atoms.effect: The move-in report is deemed correct.
atoms.cross_time: Fixes the move-in baseline used at move-out.
atoms.quote: and the report shall be deemed correct unless the tenant objects to it in writing within five days after receipt of the report.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The landlord adopts a written policy letting the tenant prepare the move-in report, or letting both prepare it jointly.
atoms.effect: A tenant-prepared report is deemed correct unless the landlord objects in writing within five days of receipt; a jointly prepared report signed by both and copied to both is deemed correct.
atoms.quote: The landlord may adopt a written policy allowing the tenant to prepare the written report of the move-in inspection, in which case the tenant shall submit a copy to the landlord, and the report shall be deemed correct unless the landlord objects thereto in writing within five days after receipt of the report.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: Damage is listed on the move-in report.
atoms.effect: The landlord need not repair it unless 55.1-1215 or 55.1-1220 requires (listed pre-existing damage is not the departing tenant's damage).
atoms.quote: If any damages are reflected on the written report, a landlord is not required to make repairs to address such damages unless required to do so under § 55.1-1215 or 55.1-1220.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The move-in report is prepared.
atoms.effect: It must disclose whether visible evidence of mold exists in readily accessible interior areas; a no-mold statement is deemed correct unless the tenant objects in writing within five days.
atoms.cross_time: Move-in baseline for mold later charged under 55.1-1227(A)(10) / 55.1-1231.
atoms.quote: If the landlord's written disclosure states that there is no visible evidence of mold in the dwelling unit, this written statement shall be deemed correct unless the tenant objects to it in writing within five days after receiving the report.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: A security deposit is demanded or received.
atoms.effect: It may not exceed two months' periodic rent in amount or value.
atoms.quote: No landlord may demand or receive a security deposit, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of two months' periodic rent.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: On the later of termination of the tenancy or the date the tenant vacates.
atoms.effect: The deposit may be applied only to: (i) accrued rent, including reasonable late charges specified in the rental agreement; (ii) damages from the tenant's noncompliance with 55.1-1227, less reasonable wear and tear; (iii) other damages or charges provided in the rental agreement; (iv) actual damages for breach under 55.1-1251. Nothing else.
judgment_terms: damages suffered by reason of noncompliance
atoms.quote: Upon termination of the tenancy or the date the tenant vacates the dwelling unit, whichever occurs last, such security deposit, whether it is property or money held by the landlord as security as provided in this section, may be applied by the landlord solely to (i) the payment of accrued rent, including the reasonable charges for late payment of rent specified in the rental agreement; (ii) the payment of the amount of damages that the landlord has suffered by reason of the tenant's noncompliance with § 55.1-1227, less reasonable wear and tear; (iii) other damages or charges as provided in the rental agreement; or (iv) actual damages for breach of the rental agreement pursuant to § 55.1-1251.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The tenancy has terminated and the tenant has vacated.
atoms.effect: Give the tenant a written notice itemizing the deposit and every deduction, damage and charge, together with any amount due to the tenant, within 45 days after the later of the termination date or the vacating date.
atoms.quote: The security deposit and any deductions, damages, and charges shall be itemized by the landlord in a written notice given to the tenant, together with any amount due to the tenant, within 45 days after the termination date of the tenancy or the date the tenant vacates the dwelling unit, whichever occurs last.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The later of termination or vacating arrives.
atoms.effect: The tenant must deliver possession of the unit to the landlord as of that date.
atoms.quote: As of the date of the termination of the tenancy or the date the tenant vacates the dwelling unit, whichever occurs last, the tenant shall be required to deliver possession of the dwelling unit to the landlord.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The termination date is before the lease (or renewal) expires, or the tenant did not give proper notice of termination.
atoms.effect: The tenant is liable for actual damages under 55.1-1251; the landlord must still give the written disposition notice within the 45-day period but may keep any deposit balance to apply against the tenant's financial obligations under the chapter or the lease.
atoms.quote: If the termination date is prior to the expiration of the rental agreement or any renewal thereof, or the tenant has not given proper notice of termination of the rental agreement, the tenant shall be liable for actual damages pursuant to § 55.1-1251, in which case, the landlord shall give written notice of security deposit disposition within the 45-day period but may retain any security balance to apply against any financial obligations of the tenant to the landlord pursuant to this chapter or the rental agreement.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The tenant fails to vacate as of termination.
atoms.effect: The landlord may file unlawful detainer under 8.01-126.
atoms.quote: If the tenant fails to vacate the dwelling unit as of the termination of the tenancy, the landlord may file an unlawful detainer action pursuant to § 8.01-126.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: More than one tenant is subject to the rental agreement, and the tenants have not each agreed otherwise in writing.
atoms.effect: Make the disposition by one check payable to all the tenants, sent to a forwarding address provided by one of them.
atoms.quote: Where there is more than one tenant subject to a rental agreement, unless otherwise agreed to in writing by each of the tenants, disposition of the security deposit shall be made with one check being payable to all such tenants and sent to a forwarding address provided by one of the tenants.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: No forwarding address has been provided.
atoms.effect: The disposition must still be made within the 45-day period, but the landlord may continue to hold the deposit in escrow.
atoms.quote: The landlord shall make the security deposit disposition within the 45-day time period required by subsection A, but if no forwarding address is provided to the landlord, the landlord may continue to hold such security deposit in escrow.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: A tenant has not provided a forwarding address that would let the landlord refund the deposit, and one year has passed since the end of the 45-day period.
atoms.effect: The landlord may remit the sum to the State Treasurer as unclaimed property on the administrator's form, giving each tenant's name, social security number if known, and last known address.
atoms.cross_time: Runs one year beyond the 45-day disposition window.
atoms.quote: If a tenant fails to provide a forwarding address to the landlord to enable the landlord to make a refund of the security deposit, upon the expiration of one year from the date of the end of the 45-day time period, the landlord may remit such sum to the State Treasurer as unclaimed property on a form prescribed by the administrator that includes the name; social security number, if known; and last known address of each tenant on the rental agreement.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.actor: landlord or managing agent who is a real estate licensee
atoms.condition: The landlord or managing agent is a real estate licensee and complies with 55.1-1226(B).
atoms.effect: That compliance is deemed compliance with 54.1-2108 and the Real Estate Board's corresponding regulations (holding an unrefunded deposit in escrow and remitting it after a year do not breach the licensee escrow rules).
atoms.quote: If the landlord or managing agent is a real estate licensee, compliance with this subsection shall be deemed compliance with § 54.1-2108 and corresponding regulations of the Real Estate Board.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The tenancy terminates with delinquent rent.
atoms.effect: The tenant is not entitled to an immediate credit of the deposit against the delinquent rent account.
atoms.quote: Nothing in this section shall be construed by a court of law or otherwise as entitling the tenant, upon the termination of the tenancy, to an immediate credit against the tenant's delinquent rent account in the amount of the security deposit.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The tenancy has ended.
atoms.effect: Apply the deposit under 55.1-1226 within the 45-day period.
atoms.quote: The landlord shall apply the security deposit in accordance with this section within the 45-day time period required by subsection A.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: Prior written notice has been given as the section requires, and a water, sewer or other utility account balance is the tenant's obligation to a third-party provider under the lease.
atoms.effect: The landlord may withhold a reasonable portion of the deposit to cover that balance; once the obligation is paid, it must give the tenant written confirmation within 10 days with payment of any balance due to the tenant.
atoms.quote: However, provided that the landlord has given prior written notice in accordance with this section, the landlord may withhold a reasonable portion of the security deposit to cover an amount of the balance due on the water, sewer, or other utility account that is an obligation of the tenant to a third-party provider under the rental agreement for the dwelling unit, and upon payment of such obligations the landlord shall provide written confirmation to the tenant within 10 days, along with payment to the tenant of any balance otherwise due to the tenant.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The landlord wants to withhold for a third-party utility balance as part of the disposition.
atoms.effect: It must have advised the tenant of the tenant's rights and obligations under the section in (i) a termination notice, (ii) a written notice confirming the vacating date, or (iii) a separate written notice at least 15 days before the disposition; any such notice is given under 55.1-1202. Without it, no utility withholding.
atoms.quote: In order to withhold such funds as part of the disposition of the security deposit, the landlord shall have so advised the tenant of his rights and obligations under this section in (i) a termination notice to the tenant in accordance with this chapter, (ii) a written notice to the tenant confirming the vacating date in accordance with this section, or (iii) a separate written notice to the tenant at least 15 days prior to the disposition of the security deposit.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The tenant gives written confirmation that the final water, sewer or other utility bill is paid.
atoms.effect: If received in time, refund within the 45-day period (unless other authorized deductions); if received after the 45 days, refund any remaining deposit held within 10 days after receiving it.
atoms.quote: If the tenant provides such written confirmation after the expiration of the 45-day period, the landlord shall refund any remaining balance of the security deposit held to the tenant within 10 days following the receipt of such written confirmation provided by the tenant.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The landlord otherwise receives confirmation that the final utility bill is paid.
atoms.effect: Refund the deposit within the 45-day period unless there are other authorized deductions.
atoms.quote: If the landlord otherwise receives confirmation of payment of the final water, sewer, or other utility bill for the dwelling unit, the landlord shall refund the security deposit, unless there are other authorized deductions, within the 45-day period.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The rental agreement provides for it and the tenant requests expedited processing in a separate written document.
atoms.effect: The landlord may make the disposition before the 45 days and charge the tenant an administrative fee for expedited processing.
atoms.quote: Nothing in this section shall be construed to prohibit the landlord from making the disposition of the security deposit prior to the 45-day period required by subsection A and charging an administrative fee to the tenant for such expedited processing, if the rental agreement so provides and the tenant requests expedited processing in a separate written document.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The landlord determines a deduction from the deposit during the tenancy, more than 30 days before the rental agreement terminates.
atoms.effect: Notify the tenant in writing within 30 days of the determination, itemizing reasons as in 55.1-1226(F); no notice is required for deductions made less than 30 days before termination.
atoms.cross_time: A deduction made mid-tenancy carries into the final disposition.
atoms.quote: Such notification shall be made within 30 days of the date of the determination of the deduction and shall itemize the reasons in the same manner as provided in subsection F. No such notification shall be required for deductions made less than 30 days prior to the termination of the rental agreement.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The landlord willfully fails to comply with 55.1-1226.
atoms.effect: The court shall order return of the deposit with actual damages and reasonable attorney fees; but if the tenant owes rent, the court orders an amount equal to the deposit credited against the rent due. "Willfully" means intentional noncompliance, not inadvertent or negligent noncompliance (VA:55.1-1226(E)-willful-meaning).
atoms.quote: If the landlord willfully fails to comply with this section, the court shall order the return of the security deposit to the tenant, together with actual damages and reasonable attorney fees, unless the tenant owes rent to the landlord, in which case the court shall order an amount equal to the security deposit credited against the rent due to the landlord.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: Damage to the premises exceeds the deposit and requires a third-party contractor, and the landlord gives the tenant written notice of that within the 45-day period.
atoms.effect: The landlord gets an additional 15 days to provide an itemization of the damages and the cost of repair.
judgment_terms: require the services of a third-party contractor
atoms.quote: In the event that damages to the premises exceed the amount of the security deposit and require the services of a third-party contractor, the landlord shall give written notice to the tenant advising him of that fact within the 45-day period required by subsection A. If notice is given as prescribed in this subsection, the landlord shall have an additional 15-day period to provide an itemization of the damages and the cost of repair.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: Always.
atoms.effect: The deposit section does not stop either party recovering other damages under chapter 12 (the landlord can pursue a balance beyond the deposit).
atoms.quote: This section shall not preclude the landlord or tenant from recovering other damages to which he may be entitled under this chapter.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.actor: holder of the landlord's interest at termination (successor landlord)
atoms.condition: The landlord's interest was transferred before the tenancy terminated.
atoms.effect: Whoever holds the landlord's interest at termination is bound by the section and must return any deposit received by the original landlord that is owed to the tenant, whether or not the deposit was transferred and regardless of contracts between original landlord and successors.
atoms.cross_time: Reaches back to deposits taken by a prior owner.
atoms.quote: The holder of the landlord's interest in the premises at the time of the termination of the tenancy, regardless of how the interest is acquired or transferred, is bound by this section and shall be required to return any security deposit received by the original landlord that is duly owed to the tenant, whether or not such security deposit is transferred with the landlord's interest by law or equity, regardless of any contractual agreements between the original landlord and his successors in interest.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The landlord has made deductions from security deposits.
atoms.effect: Keep itemized records, per tenant, of all deductions made for 55.1-1227 noncompliance or any other reason in the section, covering the preceding two years.
atoms.quote: Maintain and itemize records for each tenant of all deductions from security deposits provided for under this section that the landlord has made by reason of a tenant's noncompliance with § 55.1-1227, or for any other reason set out in this section, during the preceding two years; and

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: A tenant or the tenant's agent or attorney asks during normal business hours.
atoms.effect: Let them inspect that tenant's deduction records.
atoms.quote: Permit a tenant or his authorized agent or attorney to inspect such tenant's records of deductions at any time during normal business hours.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)

atoms.quote: Upon request by the landlord to a tenant to vacate, or within five days after receipt of notice by the landlord of the tenant's intent to vacate, the landlord shall provide written notice to the tenant of the tenant's right to be present at the landlord's inspection of the dwelling unit for the purpose of determining the amount of security deposit to be returned.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The tenant advises the landlord in writing that it wants to be present.
atoms.effect: Notify the tenant of the date and time of the inspection, which must be made within 72 hours of delivery of possession.
atoms.quote: If the tenant desires to be present when the landlord makes the inspection, he shall, in writing, so advise the landlord, who in turn shall notify the tenant of the date and time of the inspection, which must be made within 72 hours of delivery of possession.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The move-out inspection has occurred.
atoms.effect: Provide the tenant a written security deposit disposition statement including an itemized list of damages.
atoms.quote: Following the move-out inspection, the landlord shall provide the tenant with a written security deposit disposition statement, including an itemized list of damages.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The landlord discovers additional damage after the disposition has been made.
atoms.effect: The landlord may still recover it from the tenant; the tenant may put the move-out report in evidence to show the damage did not exist at the move-out inspection.
judgment_terms: whether additional damages existed at the move-out inspection
atoms.quote: If additional damages are discovered by the landlord after the security deposit disposition has been made, nothing in this section shall be construed to preclude the landlord from recovery of such damages against the tenant, provided, however, that the tenant may present into evidence a copy of the move-out report to support the tenant's position that such additional damages did not exist at the time of the move-out inspection.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The tenant has an assignee or sublessee.
atoms.effect: The landlord may hold a security deposit from only one party.
atoms.quote: If the tenant has any assignee or sublessee, the landlord shall be entitled to hold a security deposit from only one party in compliance with the provisions of this section.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The landlord requires damage insurance as a condition of tenancy and the tenant pays the premiums.
atoms.effect: Premium payments are rent, not a security deposit (so unpaid premiums are rent owed); deposit plus damage-insurance premiums may not exceed two months' periodic rent.
atoms.quote: A. A landlord may require as a condition of tenancy that a tenant have damage insurance and pay for the cost of premiums. As provided in § 55.1-1200, such payments shall not be deemed a security deposit, but shall be rent.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The tenant pays both a security deposit and damage insurance premiums.
atoms.effect: The landlord may not require both if their total exceeds two months' periodic rent.
atoms.quote: However, as provided in § 55.1-1208, the landlord shall not require a tenant to pay both a security deposit and the cost of damage insurance premiums if the total amount of any security deposit and damage insurance premiums exceeds the amount of two months' periodic rent.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The landlord obtains damage insurance on the tenant's behalf.
atoms.effect: The landlord recovers the actual cost of the coverage from the tenant and may recover administrative fees, including for a tenant opting out.
atoms.quote: The landlord shall recover from the tenant the actual costs of such insurance coverage and may recover administrative or other fees associated with administration of a damage insurance policy, including a tenant opting out of the insurance coverage provided by the landlord pursuant to this subsection.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: A tenant opts out of the landlord's damage insurance program.
atoms.effect: The landlord must allow the tenant either to provide its own damage insurance policy or to pay the full security deposit.
atoms.quote: For a tenant that opts out of the landlord's damage insurance program, the landlord shall allow such tenant to either provide their own damage insurance policy or pay the full security deposit.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The tenant pays premiums for renter's insurance obtained by the landlord.
atoms.effect: Those payments are rent, not a security deposit; after a lapse, landlord-provided coverage premiums are owed as rent until the tenant documents reinstated coverage.
atoms.quote: The tenant shall be obligated to pay for the cost of premiums for such insurance as rent or as otherwise provided herein until the tenant has provided written documentation to the landlord showing that the tenant has reinstated his own renter's insurance coverage.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The landlord provides other insurance coverage for the premises or a self-insurance escrow.
atoms.effect: It may recover, as part of rent, the tenant's prorated share of actual costs and associated administrative fees.
atoms.quote: Nothing in this section shall be construed to prohibit the landlord from recovering from the tenant, as part of the rent, the tenant's prorated share of the actual costs of other insurance coverages provided by the landlord relative to the premises, or the tenant's prorated share of a self-insurance program held in an escrow account by the landlord, including the landlord's administrative or other fees associated with the administration of such coverages.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The landlord receives prepaid rent.
atoms.effect: Place it in escrow in a federally insured depository by the end of the fifth business day after receipt; keep it there until due; do not remove it without the tenant's written consent unless the landlord has become entitled to it. Unearned prepaid rent is refundable at termination.
atoms.quote: If a landlord receives prepaid rent, it shall be placed in an escrow account in a federally insured depository authorized to do business in Virginia by the end of the fifth business day following receipt and shall remain in the account until such time as the prepaid rent becomes due.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: A written rental agreement is prepared.
