atoms.cross_time: Lease-formation term that limits what deposits and rent can be charged at the end.
atoms.quote: No additional security deposits or rent shall be charged unless they are listed below or incorporated into this agreement by way of a separate addendum after execution of this rental agreement.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28; same text in the version effective 2027-07-01
atoms.condition: A late charge is assessed.
atoms.effect: No late charge unless the written rental agreement provides for it; it may not exceed the lesser of 10% of the periodic rent or 10% of the remaining balance due and owed.
atoms.quote: A landlord shall not charge a tenant for late payment of rent unless such charge is provided for in the written rental agreement. No such late charge shall exceed the lesser of 10 percent of the periodic rent or 10 percent of the remaining balance due and owed by the tenant.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28; same text in the version effective 2027-07-01
atoms.condition: The landlord did not offer a written rental agreement.
atoms.effect: The tenancy exists by operation of law: rent due on the 1st and late after the 5th; a late charge only "as provided in this chapter", which requires a written rental agreement term, so none is chargeable until the parties sign one (VA:55.1-1204(C)-late-charge); deposit at most two months' rent; 12-month term.
atoms.quote: If the rent is paid by the tenant after the fifth day of any given month, the landlord shall be entitled to charge a late charge as provided in this chapter;

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28; same text in the version effective 2027-07-01
atoms.condition: The landlord receives a tenant's written request for a statement of charges and payments.
atoms.effect: Within 10 business days, provide a written statement of all debits and credits over the tenancy or the past 12 months, whichever is shorter.
atoms.quote: If the landlord receives from a tenant a written request for a written statement of charges and payments, he shall provide the tenant with a written statement showing all debits and credits over the tenancy or the past 12 months, whichever is shorter. The landlord shall provide such written statement within 10 business days of receiving the request.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28; same text in the version effective 2027-07-01
atoms.condition: The landlord has not provided the tenant the statement of tenant rights and responsibilities.
atoms.effect: The landlord may not file or maintain a court action against the tenant for an alleged lease violation (bars suing a former tenant for the balance until provided).
atoms.cross_time: Lease-formation duty that conditions later collection suits.
atoms.quote: However, the landlord shall not file or maintain an action, including any summons for unlawful detainer, against the tenant in a court of law for any alleged lease violation until he has provided the tenant with the statement of tenant rights and responsibilities.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28; same text in the version effective 2027-07-01
atoms.condition: Either party changes a rental agreement term unilaterally.
atoms.effect: The change is invalid unless notice is given per the lease or law and both parties consent in writing (a charge added without written consent is not a lease charge).
atoms.quote: No unilateral change in the terms of a rental agreement by a landlord or tenant shall be valid unless (i) notice of the change is given in accordance with the terms of the rental agreement or as otherwise required by law and (ii) both parties consent in writing to the change.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28; same text in the version effective 2027-07-01
atoms.condition: The landlord charges a fee to collect or process a payment of rent, deposit or other fees (including a final balance).
atoms.effect: Allowed only if a fee-free alternative payment method is offered; and card/electronic processing fees may not exceed the actual out-of-pocket third-party cost.
atoms.quote: No landlord shall charge a tenant any fee for the collection or processing of any payment of rent, security deposit, or any other fees, unless the landlord offers an alternative method of payment that does not include additional fees.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28; same text in the version effective 2027-07-01
atoms.condition: Termination of a tenancy.
atoms.effect: Unless the written lease says otherwise, tenancies are week-to-week (weekly rent) or month-to-month; terminations follow 55.1-1253 unless the lease provides a different notice period.
atoms.quote: Terminations of tenancies shall be governed by § 55.1-1253 unless the rental agreement provides for a different notice period.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28; same text in the version effective 2027-07-01 (Acts 2026 c. 783/784)
atoms.actor: owner, manager or operator of residential building
atoms.condition: Energy or water/sewer submetering or energy allocation equipment is used, and the charges are agreed in the lease.
atoms.effect: The owner may charge and collect service charges, including account move-out fees, to cover actual third-party administrative and billing costs, and a late charge of up to $5 if payment is late (due no less than 15 days after the bill is mailed or delivered).
atoms.quote: The owner, manager, or operator of such residential building may charge and collect from the tenant additional service charges, including monthly billing fees, account set-up fees, or account move-out fees, to cover the actual costs of administrative expenses and billing charged to the residential building owner, manager, or operator by a third-party provider of such services, provided that such charges are agreed to by the residential building owner and the tenant in the rental agreement or lease.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28; same text in the version effective 2027-07-01 (Acts 2026 c. 783/784)
atoms.actor: owner, manager or operator of residential building
atoms.condition: A ratio utility billing system (RUBS) is used and charges are agreed in the lease.
atoms.effect: Allocated utility charges, move-out and similar service charges (actual third-party costs) and a late charge of up to $5 may be collected; for a residential multifamily unit the late charge is deemed rent.
atoms.quote: The late charge shall be deemed rent (i) as defined in § 55.1-1200 if a ratio utility billing system is used in a residential multifamily dwelling unit subject to this chapter or (ii) as defined in § 55.1-1300 if a ratio utility billing system is used in a manufactured home park subject to the Manufactured Home Lot Rental Act (§ 55.1-1300 et seq.).

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28; same text in the version effective 2027-07-01 (Acts 2026 c. 783/784)
atoms.actor: owner, manager or operator of residential building
atoms.condition: Local government fees are allocated among tenants under a program clearly stated in the lease.
atoms.effect: Those fees and related administrative charges are rent under 55.1-1200.
atoms.quote: If the building is residential and is subject to (i) this chapter, such local government fees and administrative expenses shall be deemed to be rent as defined in § 55.1-1200 or (ii) the Manufactured Home Lot Rental Act (§ 55.1-1300 et seq.), such local government fees and administrative expenses shall be deemed to be rent as defined in § 55.1-1300.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.condition: On or after 2027-07-01, the building uses submetering, energy allocation or RUBS.
atoms.effect: Records must include how monthly billing fees are calculated and a per-tenant history of billing-fee payments over the tenancy or past 12 months, whichever is shorter.
atoms.quote: Such records shall include a description of how monthly energy and utility billing fees are calculated and a history of billing fee payments for each tenant over the duration of the tenancy or the past 12 months, whichever is shorter.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: During the tenancy, in addition to the rental agreement.
atoms.effect: The tenant owes the listed maintenance duties (1-15). Damage the landlord suffers from breach of them, less reasonable wear and tear, is deductible under 55.1-1226(A)(ii).

atoms.condition: The tenant pays utilities directly to a provider under the lease.
atoms.effect: Use utilities and facilities reasonably and keep tenant-paid utility service paid and on for the whole term.
atoms.quote: Use in a reasonable manner all utilities and all electrical, plumbing, sanitary, heating, ventilating, air-conditioning, and other facilities and appliances, including an elevator in a multifamily premises, and keep all utility services paid for by the tenant to the utility service provider or its agent on at all times during the term of the rental agreement;

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)

atoms.condition: During the tenancy.
atoms.effect: Not deliberately or negligently destroy, deface, damage, impair or remove any part of the premises, or permit anyone to do so.
atoms.quote: Not deliberately or negligently destroy, deface, damage, impair, or remove any part of the premises or permit any person, whether known by the tenant or not, to do so;

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: Pest treatment was needed because of the tenant's unreasonable delay in reporting, or the tenant's fault in failing to prevent infestation.
atoms.effect: The tenant is financially responsible for the added (or full) treatment cost.
atoms.quote: Be financially responsible for the added cost of treatment or extermination due to the tenant's unreasonable delay in reporting the existence of any insects or pests and be financially responsible for the cost of treatment or extermination due to the tenant's fault in failing to prevent infestation of any insects or pests in the area occupied; and

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The building-code duty in (A)(1) is greater than another (A) duty.
atoms.effect: The tenant's duty is measured by (A)(1).
atoms.quote: If the duty imposed by subdivision A 1 is greater than any duty imposed by any other subdivision of that subsection, the tenant's duty shall be determined by reference to subdivision A 1.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The tenancy terminates by expiration or tenant default.
atoms.effect: Promptly vacate, remove all personal property, and leave the premises in good and clean order, reasonable wear and tear excepted (the baseline for cleaning and damage charges).
atoms.quote: At the termination of the term of tenancy, whether by expiration of the rental agreement or by reason of default by the tenant, the tenant shall promptly vacate the premises, removing all items of personal property and leaving the premises in good and clean order, reasonable wear and tear excepted.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The tenant fails to vacate at termination.
atoms.effect: The landlord may sue for possession and damages, including reasonable attorney fees.
atoms.quote: If the tenant fails to vacate, the landlord may bring an action for possession and damages, including reasonable attorney fees.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The tenant's breach of 55.1-1227 or the lease materially affecting health and safety can be remedied by repair, replacement or cleaning, and the landlord gives the required written notice (or acts in an emergency).
atoms.effect: The landlord (or a third party it engages) performs the work and submits an itemized bill for actual and reasonable cost, due as rent on the next due date or, if the lease has terminated, for immediate payment.
atoms.quote: If there is a violation by the tenant of § 55.1-1227 or the rental agreement materially affecting health and safety that can be remedied by repair, replacement of a damaged item, or cleaning, the landlord shall send a written notice to the tenant specifying the breach and stating that the landlord will enter the dwelling unit and perform the work in a workmanlike manner and submit an itemized bill for the actual and reasonable cost for such work to the tenant, which shall be due as rent on the next rent due date or, if the rental agreement has terminated, for immediate payment.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The tenant installed security devices during the tenancy.
atoms.effect: At termination the tenant pays the landlord the reasonable cost of removing them and repairing damaged areas.
atoms.quote: Upon termination of the tenancy, the tenant is responsible for payment to the landlord for reasonable costs incurred for the removal of all such devices and repairs to all damaged areas.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The lease so provides and the tenant, without reasonable justification, refused to let the landlord show the unit for sale or lease.
atoms.effect: The landlord may recover damages, costs and reasonable attorney fees.
atoms.quote: If the rental agreement so provides and if a tenant without reasonable justification declines to permit the landlord or managing agent to exhibit the dwelling unit for sale or lease, the landlord may recover damages, costs, and reasonable attorney fees against such tenant.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: Locks or security devices were installed under a protective-order request.
atoms.effect: At termination the tenant pays reasonable removal and repair costs.
atoms.quote: Upon termination of the tenancy, the tenant shall be responsible for payment to the landlord of the reasonable costs incurred for the removal of all such devices installed and repairs to all damaged areas.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The tenant refused lawful access.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The landlord relocates the tenant for mold remediation.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: A periodic tenancy is to end, or the parties want early termination.
atoms.effect: Week-to-week: written notice at least 7 days before the next rent due date; month-to-month: at least 30 days before the next rent due date unless the lease sets another period. atoms.quote: The landlord and the tenant may agree in writing to an early termination of a rental agreement. In the event that no such agreement is reached, the provisions of § 55.1-1251 shall control.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)

atoms.quote: The landlord may include in the rental agreement a reasonable liquidated damage penalty, not to exceed an amount equal to 150 percent of the per diem of the monthly rent, for each day the tenant remains in the dwelling unit after the termination date specified in the landlord's notice.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The tenant stays on with the landlord's agreement after termination and no new lease is signed.
atoms.effect: The old lease terms govern the holdover or month-to-month tenancy; rent changes only by written notice effective the next due date at least 30 days later.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)

atoms.condition: The rental agreement is terminated.
atoms.effect: The landlord may claim possession and rent, and separately actual damages for breach, reasonable attorney fees as provided in 55.1-1245, and the cost of serving notices or process (capped at the 55.1-1247 amount).
atoms.quote: If the rental agreement is terminated, the landlord may have a claim for possession and for rent and a separate claim for actual damages for breach of the rental agreement, reasonable attorney fees as provided in § 55.1-1245, and the cost of service of any notice under § 55.1-1245 or 55.1-1415 or process by a sheriff or private process server, which cost shall not exceed the amount authorized by § 55.1-1247, and such claims may be enforced, without limitation, by initiating an action for unlawful entry or detainer.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The tenant breached and the tenancy ended early.
atoms.effect: Actual damages may include rent that would have accrued until the lease term expires or a new tenancy begins, whichever comes first; the landlord's duty to mitigate is not diminished.
atoms.quote: Actual damages for breach of the rental agreement may include a claim for rent that would have accrued until the expiration of the term of the rental agreement or until a tenancy pursuant to a new rental agreement commences, whichever occurs first, provided that nothing contained in this section shall diminish the duty of the landlord to mitigate actual damages for breach of the rental agreement.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The landlord seeks a post-possession judgment for actual damages.
atoms.effect: It may not seek a judgment for accelerated rent through the end of the term.
atoms.quote: In obtaining post-possession judgments for actual damages as defined in this section, the landlord shall not seek a judgment for accelerated rent through the end of the term of the tenancy.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The tenant vacates voluntarily or by writ of eviction.
atoms.effect: Deposits are credited to the tenant's account under 55.1-1226 (a court may enter a money judgment in unlawful detainer without a deposit credit).
atoms.quote: Upon the tenant vacating the premises either voluntarily or by a writ of eviction, security deposits shall be credited to the tenant's account by the landlord in accordance with the requirements of § 55.1-1226.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28; same text in all three versions
atoms.condition: Material noncompliance by the tenant, or a 55.1-1227 violation materially affecting health and safety.
atoms.effect: The landlord may serve written notice that the lease terminates on a date at least 30 days after receipt unless the breach is remedied in 21 days.
atoms.quote: Except as otherwise provided in this chapter, if there is a material noncompliance by the tenant with the rental agreement or a violation of § 55.1-1227 materially affecting health and safety, the landlord may serve a written notice on the tenant specifying the acts and omissions constituting the breach and stating that the rental agreement will terminate upon a date not less than 30 days after receipt of the notice if the breach is not remedied in 21 days and that the rental agreement shall terminate as provided in the notice.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28; same opening text in later versions
atoms.condition: Rent is unpaid when due and the tenant does not pay within 14 days after written notice of nonpayment and intent to terminate.
atoms.effect: The landlord may terminate and seek possession under 55.1-1251 (termination date anchors the deposit clock).
atoms.quote: If rent is unpaid when due, and the tenant fails to pay rent within 14 days after written notice is served on him notifying the tenant of his nonpayment, and of the landlord's intention to terminate the rental agreement if the rent is not paid within the 14-day period, the landlord may terminate the rental agreement and proceed to obtain possession of the premises as provided in § 55.1-1251.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: Rent was paid by a bad check or rejected EFT and the landlord gave notice under 55.1-1202 (which may be in the 14-day notice).
atoms.effect: The landlord may seek costs or attorney fees under 8.01-27.1 or civil recovery under 8.01-27.2 as part of damages in unlawful detainer.
atoms.quote: Nothing shall be construed to prevent a landlord from seeking an award of costs or attorney fees under § 8.01-27.1 or civil recovery under § 8.01-27.2, as a part of other damages requested on the unlawful detainer filed pursuant to § 8.01-126, provided that the landlord has given notice in accordance with § 55.1-1202, which notice may be included in the 14-day termination notice provided in accordance with this section.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.actor: landlord owning more than four units (or >10% interest in more than four)
atoms.condition: On or after 2027-07-01, the tenant entered a payment plan offered under 55.1-1245(G) and makes timely plan payments.
atoms.effect: No additional late fees may be charged during the plan period on the amount covered by the plan.
atoms.quote: The landlord shall not charge any additional late fees during the payment plan period in connection with the unpaid rental amount for which the tenant entered into the payment plan so long as the tenant makes timely payments in accordance with the terms of the payment plan.

atoms.instrument: Acts of Assembly 2026, chapter 1105

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 as subsection H; re-lettered J from 2027-07-01 with same text (Acts 2026 c. 1105)
atoms.condition: The tenant breached the rental agreement or failed to comply.
atoms.effect: Whether or not a suit is filed, the landlord is entitled to recover: rent due as contracted; other contracted charges and fees; contracted late charges; reasonable attorney fees as contracted or provided by law; costs of the proceeding only if court action has been filed; and contracted damages to the unit or premises. This defines the balance a manager may state and pursue.
atoms.quote: In the event of a breach of the rental agreement or noncompliance by the tenant, the landlord shall be entitled to recover from the tenant the following, regardless of whether a lawsuit is filed or an order is obtained from a court: (i) rent due and owing as contracted for in the rental agreement, (ii) other charges and fees as contracted for in the rental agreement, (iii) late charges contracted for in the rental agreement, (iv) reasonable attorney fees as contracted for in the rental agreement or as provided by law, (v) costs of the proceeding as contracted for in the rental agreement or as provided by law only if court action has been filed, and (vi) damages to the dwelling unit or premises as contracted for in the rental agreement.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 as subsection I; re-lettered K from 2027-07-01 with same text
atoms.condition: A suit on the breach is pending and the landlord prevails.
atoms.effect: The court awards a money judgment that may include rent as of the court date, contracted charges, late charges, reasonable attorney fees (unless the tenant proves by a preponderance that its failure to pay or vacate was reasonable), costs, and damages.
judgment_terms: failure to pay rent or vacate was reasonable
atoms.quote: (iv) reasonable attorney fees as contracted for in the rental agreement or as provided by law, unless in any such action the tenant proves by a preponderance of the evidence that the tenant's failure to pay rent or vacate was reasonable;

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: A service member qualifies under 55.1-1235(A) (PCS, long TDY, discharge, quarters order, stop movement).
atoms.effect: Terminates by written notice effective on a stated date at least 30 days after the first rent due date following the notice, furnishing a copy of orders or a commanding officer letter before termination.
atoms.quote: Tenants who qualify to terminate a rental agreement pursuant to subsection A shall do so by serving on the landlord a written notice of termination to be effective on a date stated in such written notice, such date to be not less than 30 days after the first date on which the next rental payment is due and payable after the date on which the written notice is given.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The tenant terminates under 55.1-1235.
atoms.effect: No liquidated damages may be charged.
atoms.quote: The landlord may not charge any liquidated damages.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The tenant terminates under 55.1-1235.
atoms.effect: The 55.1-1227 maintenance obligations (so damage deductions) are unaffected.
atoms.quote: Nothing in this section shall affect the tenant's obligations established by § 55.1-1227.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The tenant qualifies under 55.1-1236(A) (protective order, conviction or charge).
atoms.effect: Termination is effective 28 days after the tenant serves written notice, with a copy of the order or charging document.
atoms.quote: A tenant who qualifies to terminate such tenant's obligations under a rental agreement pursuant to subsection A shall do so by serving on the landlord a written notice of termination to be effective 28 days after the tenant serves the termination notice on the landlord.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: Termination under 55.1-1236.
atoms.effect: Rent remains payable as the lease requires through the effective date.
atoms.quote: The rent shall be payable at such time as would otherwise have been required by the terms of the rental agreement through the effective date of the termination as provided in subsection B.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: Termination under 55.1-1236.
atoms.effect: No liquidated damages.
atoms.quote: The landlord may not charge any liquidated damages.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: A victim terminates under 55.1-1236.
atoms.effect: The victim's 55.1-1227 duties run through the effective date; co-tenants on the lease remain responsible for rent for the rest of the term.
atoms.quote: Any co-tenants on the lease with the victim shall remain responsible for the rent for the balance of the term of the rental agreement.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The perpetrator is the remaining sole tenant.
atoms.effect: The landlord may terminate and collect actual damages for the termination from the perpetrator under 55.1-1251.
atoms.quote: If the perpetrator is the remaining sole tenant obligated on the rental agreement, the landlord may terminate the rental agreement and collect actual damages for such termination against the perpetrator pursuant to § 55.1-1251.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The tenant abandons the unit.
atoms.effect: The rental agreement is deemed terminated by the landlord as of the date of abandonment; that is the termination date for 55.1-1226 (VA:55.1-1226(A)-clock-abandonment). Where abandonment is established only through the 55.1-1249 notice, termination falls on the seventh day after the notice (VA:55.1-1226(A)-clock-abandonment-notice).
atoms.quote: The rental agreement is deemed to be terminated by the landlord as of the date of abandonment by the tenant.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The landlord cannot determine whether the tenant has abandoned the premises.
atoms.effect: Serve written notice under 55.1-1202 requiring the tenant to state in writing within seven days an intent to remain; absent that (or other knowledge of occupancy), after seven days abandonment is rebuttably presumed and the lease is deemed terminated on that date.
judgment_terms: otherwise determines that the tenant remains in occupancy
atoms.quote: Unless the landlord receives written notice from the tenant or otherwise determines that the tenant remains in occupancy of the premises, upon the expiration of seven days from the date of the landlord's notice to the tenant, there shall be a rebuttable presumption that the premises has been abandoned by the tenant, and the rental agreement shall be deemed to terminate on that date.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The tenant abandoned (or failed to give a required extended-absence notice).
atoms.effect: The landlord must mitigate damages under 55.1-1251; if the lease requires notice of absences over seven days and none was given, the landlord may recover actual damages.
atoms.quote: The landlord shall mitigate damages in accordance with § 55.1-1251.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The sole tenant under a written lease, still residing in the unit, dies.
atoms.effect: The lease is deemed terminated as of the date of death (no court order needed); the estate remains liable for actual damages under 55.1-1251 and the landlord must mitigate.
atoms.quote: The rental agreement is deemed to be terminated by the landlord as of the date of death of the tenant who is the sole tenant under a written rental agreement still residing in the dwelling unit, and the landlord shall not be required to seek an order of possession from a court of competent jurisdiction. The estate of the tenant shall remain liable for actual damages under § 55.1-1251, and the landlord shall mitigate such damages.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The sole tenant has died and the landlord has verified the contact person's identification.
atoms.effect: The authorized contact named in the lease or application may access the unit and tenant records, claim the personal property left in the unit, and deal with the landlord on the deceased tenant's affairs (including receiving the 55.1-1226 itemization). The contact is not thereby the payee of the refund (VA:55.1-1256(B)-contact-not-payee).
atoms.quote: Thereafter, the authorized contact person identified in the rental application, lease agreement, or other landlord document may (i) have access to the dwelling unit or the premises and to the tenant records maintained by the landlord and (ii) rightfully claim the personal property of the deceased tenant and otherwise handle the affairs of the deceased tenant with the landlord.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28; same text as subsection E from 2027-01-01 (Acts 2026 c. 1117)
atoms.condition: The lease is terminated because of fire or casualty damage.
atoms.effect: Return all security deposits under 55.1-1226 and prepaid rent plus accrued interest recoverable by law, unless the landlord reasonably believes the tenant, an authorized occupant, or guest caused the damage, in which case give a written statement for the security and prepaid rent and recover actual damages under 55.1-1251. Rent is prorated as of the casualty date.
atoms.quote: If the rental agreement is terminated, the landlord shall return all security deposits in accordance with § 55.1-1226 and prepaid rent, plus accrued interest, recoverable by law unless the landlord reasonably believes that the tenant, an authorized occupant, or a guest or invitee of the tenant was the cause of the damage or casualty, in which case the landlord shall provide a written statement to the tenant for the security and prepaid rent, plus accrued interest based upon the damage or casualty, and may recover actual damages sustained pursuant to § 55.1-1251.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.condition: Fire or casualty substantially impairs enjoyment or repairs require vacating.
atoms.effect: Tenant terminates by vacating and serving notice within 14 days (termination as of vacating date); landlord terminates by 14 days' notice (termination at end of notice period).
atoms.quote: The tenant may terminate the rental agreement by vacating the premises and within 14 days thereafter, serving on the landlord a written notice of his intention to terminate the rental agreement, in which case the rental agreement terminates as of the date of vacating.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.condition: On or after 2027-01-01, fire or casualty substantially impairs use and enjoyment or repairs require vacating.
atoms.effect: Tenant: vacate and serve notice within 21 days (terminates as of vacating). Landlord: 21 days' notice, only after meeting/attempting to meet the tenant and offering an available comparable unit, or after determining the tenant's 55.1-1227 violation caused the damage; tenant may request reevaluation within 7 days.
atoms.quote: The tenant may terminate the rental agreement by vacating the premises and, within 21 days thereafter, serving on the landlord a written notice of his intention to terminate the rental agreement, in which case the rental agreement terminates as of the date of vacating.

atoms.instrument: Acts of Assembly 2026, chapter 1117

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The lease is terminated because of the landlord's noncompliance.
atoms.effect: Return the security deposit under 55.1-1226.
atoms.quote: If the rental agreement is terminated due to the landlord's noncompliance, the landlord shall return the security deposit in accordance with § 55.1-1226.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: At the start of the tenancy a serious health/safety condition exists and the tenant gives written termination notice within seven days of the scheduled possession date, and the landlord does not object under (B).
atoms.effect: Refund all deposits and rent paid on or before the 15th business day after the later of delivery of the notice or vacating.
judgment_terms: fire hazard or serious threat to the life, health, or safety
atoms.quote: Unless the landlord asserts, pursuant to subsection B, that the tenant's termination of the rental agreement is unjustified, the landlord shall refund all deposits and rent paid by the tenant to the tenant on or before the fifteenth business day following the day on which (i) the termination notice is delivered to the landlord or (ii) the tenant vacates the dwelling unit, whichever occurs later.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The landlord contends the tenant's 55.1-1234.1 termination is unjustified.
atoms.effect: Give written notice of refusal with reasons within 15 business days after the termination notice is delivered.
atoms.quote: If a tenant terminates a rental agreement pursuant to subsection A and the landlord asserts that the tenant is unjustified in his termination of the rental agreement, the landlord shall provide written notice to the tenant of his refusal to accept the tenant's termination notice, along with the reasons for such refusal, within 15 business days following the date on which such termination notice is delivered to the landlord.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The landlord failed to give the foreclosure/default notice and the tenant terminated on at least five business days' notice.
atoms.effect: Make disposition of the deposit under law or the lease, whichever applies.
atoms.quote: If the tenant terminates the rental agreement, the landlord shall make disposition of the tenant's security deposit in accordance with law or the provisions of the rental agreement, whichever is applicable.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The unit is bought at foreclosure for a purpose other than the buyer's primary residence.
atoms.effect: The buyer takes subject to the lease; the tenant may stay for the remaining term (successor may terminate under 55.1-1245 or the lease).
atoms.quote: If the successor in interest acquires the dwelling unit for any other purpose, the successor in interest shall acquire the dwelling unit subject to the rental agreement and the tenant shall be permitted to occupy the dwelling unit for the remaining term of the lease, provided, however, that the successor in interest may terminate the rental agreement pursuant to § 55.1-1245 or the terms of the rental agreement.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: No managing agent is designated in the lease and the successor owner has not yet given written notice of where to pay rent.
atoms.effect: The tenant still owes rent but may not be held delinquent or charged a late charge until that notice is given.
atoms.quote: Where there is not a managing agent designated in the rental agreement, the tenant shall remain obligated for payment of the rent but shall not be held to be delinquent or assessed a late charge until the successor owner provides written notice identifying the name, address, and telephone number of the party to which the rent should be paid.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The landlord willfully fails to deliver possession and the tenant terminates on at least five days' written notice.
atoms.effect: Return all prepaid rent and security deposits (rent abates until possession).
atoms.quote: If the landlord willfully fails to deliver possession of the dwelling unit to the tenant, then rent abates until possession is delivered, and the tenant may (i) terminate the rental agreement upon at least five days' written notice to the landlord, upon which termination the landlord shall return all prepaid rent and security deposits, or (ii) demand performance of the rental agreement by the landlord.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The landlord failed to disclose known unremediated defective drywall (or, under 55.1-1219, uncleaned methamphetamine manufacture) and the tenant terminates within 60 days of discovery.
atoms.effect: Termination is effective the later of 15 days after mailing the notice or the paid-through date, but never more than one month after mailing; other rights and duties (including deposit disposition) are unaffected.
atoms.quote: Such termination shall be effective as of (i) 15 days after the date of the mailing of the notice or (ii) the date through which rent has been paid, whichever is later. In no event, however, shall the effective date of the termination exceed one month from the date of mailing.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The landlord unlawfully excluded the tenant, interrupted essential services, or made the premises unsafe, and the tenant petitions.
atoms.effect: At the full hearing the court may terminate the lease at the tenant's request and order return of all of the deposit under 55.1-1226; the tenant recovers actual damages, statutory damages of the greater of $5,000 or four months' rent, and reasonable attorney fees.
atoms.quote: At the full hearing, the court may terminate the rental agreement upon request of the tenant and order the landlord to return all of the security deposit in accordance with § 55.1-1226.
atoms.version_note: history line: 2021, Sp. Sess. I, cc. 403, 404.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The tenant had notified the landlord of a building-code violation posing substantial risk, and the unit was condemned as a result.
atoms.effect: The landlord is liable for actual damages and must return unearned prepaid rent, the security deposit, and any rent paid after condemnation.
judgment_terms: substantial risk to the health, safety, or welfare
atoms.quote: The landlord shall also return to the tenant any (i) prepaid rent that had not become due as of the date of condemnation, (ii) security deposit, or (iii) rent paid, if any, to the landlord subsequent to the unit being condemned.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The condemnation was caused by the deliberate or negligent act of the tenant, occupant or guest, or an act of God, or the lease was properly terminated under 55.1-1240.
atoms.effect: No 55.1-1243.2 liability.
judgment_terms: deliberate or negligent act or omission
atoms.quote: No landlord shall be liable pursuant to this section if:

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28; same sentence in the version effective 2027-01-01
atoms.condition: The landlord terminates on a ground that defeats a retaliation claim.
atoms.effect: Maintaining that action does not release the landlord from its deposit liability under 55.1-1226.
atoms.quote: The maintenance of the action provided in this section does not release the landlord from liability under § 55.1-1226.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: Personal property remains after the lease has terminated and possession has been delivered, and the landlord gave one of: (i) a termination notice stating items left would be disposed of within 24 hours after termination; (ii) a 55.1-1249 notice with that statement; or (iii) a separate written notice stating disposal within 24 hours after a 10-day period.
atoms.effect: The landlord may treat the property as abandoned and dispose of it as it sees fit; the tenant may remove it at reasonable times until disposal. Notices go under 55.1-1202.
atoms.quote: If any items of personal property are left in the dwelling unit, the premises, or any storage area provided by the landlord after the rental agreement has terminated and delivery of possession has occurred, the landlord may consider such property to be abandoned.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)
atoms.condition: The landlord sells abandoned property.
atoms.effect: Pay the proceeds to the tenant's account and apply them to amounts the tenant owes, including reasonable costs of selling, storing or safekeeping; any remainder is treated as a security deposit under 55.1-1226.
atoms.quote: If the landlord received any funds from any sale of abandoned property as provided in this section, the landlord shall pay such funds to the account of the tenant and apply the funds to any amounts due the landlord by the tenant, including the reasonable costs incurred by the landlord in selling, storing, or safekeeping such property. If any such funds are remaining after application, the remaining funds shall be treated as a security deposit under the provisions of § 55.1-1226.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (version start date not fixed; see version_note)

atoms.condition: A tenant seeks the 55.1-1226(E) remedy (return of the deposit with actual damages and reasonable attorney fees) for the landlord's noncompliance with 55.1-1226.
atoms.effect: "Willfully fails to comply" means the landlord intentionally did the act, or intentionally made the omission, that is the noncompliance: for example, deciding to keep a refund that is owed, deciding not to send the itemization, deciding to deduct an item that 55.1-1226(A) does not permit, or deciding to ignore the 45-day period. Knowledge that the act violates the statute is not required, and ill will is not required. Noncompliance that results from inadvertence or negligence (a clerical miss, a lost letter, a miscounted day, a mistaken belief about the facts) is not willful. The tenant bears the burden of proving willfulness by a preponderance of the evidence; the finder of fact decides it from the whole record.
atoms.quote: the tenant must adduce evidence that the act or omission that caused the interruption was intentional rather than merely inadvertent or negligent

construction.quote: we conclude that to establish that the landlord
To discover the plain and ordinary meaning of everyday language, we consult general-purpose dictionaries.
Intent in a civil context only requires that a person intended his actions; there is no requirement that the person have knowledge that his actions were wrongful.
when it is intentional
I conclude that Landlord did not willfully fail to comply with the VRLTA but was, at most, negligently noncompliant.

atoms.reasoning: The Court of Appeals of Virginia, in a published opinion (Turner v. Massie MHP, 2024), construed "willfully" in 55.1-1243.1, a section of the same chapter 12, as requiring that the landlord's act or omission be intentional rather than inadvertent or negligent, with no need for ill will, and placed the burden of proof on the tenant. Sections of one chapter are read together and the same word carries the same meaning, so that construction governs 55.1-1226(E). It rests on the Supreme Court of Virginia's civil-intent rule (Osman v. Osman, 2013: civil intent requires only that the person intended the act, not knowledge that it was wrongful) and its statement that conduct is willful when it is intentional (Suffolk City School Board v. Wahlstrom, 2023). Turner's added element for 55.1-1243.1, knowledge of a strong probability of interrupting service, tracks that section's result-based wording ("caused the interruption"); 55.1-1226(E) is conduct-based ("fails to comply"), so the intentional noncompliance itself is the willful act. The one circuit decision on 55.1-1226(E) (Reed v. Smith, 2015) draws the same line: a landlord that was at most negligent did not willfully fail to comply. The appellate construction and the circuit decision agree, so there is no conflict to adjudicate.

construction.quote: I conclude that Landlord did not willfully fail to comply with the VRLTA but was, at most, negligently noncompliant.

atoms.reasoning: 55.1-1226(E) attaches its special remedy only to willful noncompliance, and the same subsection preserves each party's other damages. A non-willful failure therefore leaves the parties with their ordinary claims: the tenant recovers what 55.1-1226(A) did not allow the landlord to keep, and the landlord pursues rent and damages. Reed v. Smith (circuit, 2015) applied this split.

When the language of a statute is unambiguous, we are bound by the plain meaning of that language.
every part of a statute is presumed to have some effect and no part will be considered meaningless unless absolutely necessary

atoms.reasoning: 1-210(E) is plain: it covers any "act" that an act of the General Assembly requires to be performed by a prescribed period, and it names two alternatives, an act to be performed and an action to be filed. The government-office words attach only to the separate office-closure trigger. Subsections (B) and (C) are expressly confined to acts "during the course of a judicial proceeding" and to bringing a "legal action"; (E) carries no such limit, and reading one into it would erase the difference the General Assembly drew and make the words "an act be performed" redundant with "an action be filed". 1-202 makes the chapter's rules govern every act of the General Assembly unless inconsistent with manifest intent, and nothing in chapter 12 displaces 1-210. Under the Supreme Court of Virginia's plain-meaning rule (Windmill Meadows, 2014) and its rule against surplusage (Hubbard, 1998), (E) reaches a landlord's 45-day deadline. atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.condition: A tenant moves out before the tenancy's scheduled end without a written early-termination agreement.
atoms.effect: "Abandonment" is the tenant's giving up of possession with the intent not to return. It occurs on the date the tenant both leaves and shows that intent: e.g. moves out and returns the keys, or moves out and tells the landlord in writing that the tenant has left. Leaving while keeping the keys, leaving belongings, or continuing to treat the unit as home is not by itself abandonment; where the landlord cannot tell, the 55.1-1249 notice procedure decides it.
atoms.quote: The rental agreement is deemed to be terminated by the landlord as of the date of abandonment by the tenant.

construction.quote: to give up with the intent of never again claiming a right or interest in
To discover the plain and ordinary meaning of everyday language, we consult general-purpose dictionaries.

If the landlord cannot determine whether the premises has been abandoned by the tenant, the landlord shall serve written notice on the tenant in accordance with § 55.1-1202 requiring the tenant to give written notice to the landlord within seven days that the tenant intends to remain in occupancy of the premises.

atoms.reasoning: Chapter 12 does not define "abandonment", so it takes its ordinary meaning from a general-purpose dictionary, the method the Virginia appellate courts use (Tomlin, quoted in Turner): to give up with the intent of never again claiming a right. 55.1-1249 itself makes intent the test: its notice procedure applies only when the landlord "cannot determine" abandonment, and a tenant who answers that it intends to remain has not abandoned. Returning the keys after moving out is the clearest act of giving up possession with intent not to return.

elect to enter and determine the lease

atoms.reasoning: At common law a landlord whose tenant abandoned could refuse the surrender and hold the tenant for rent, or elect to re-enter and end the lease (Crowder, 1920). For residential tenancies the General Assembly altered that rule (1-200): 55.1-1249 deems the rental agreement terminated as of the date of abandonment, and 55.1-1251 turns rent for the rest of the term into a damages claim limited by mitigation. 55.1-1226(A) expressly contemplates a termination date before the lease expires and still requires the disposition within 45 days, with the balance kept against the tenant's obligations. Read as a whole, the statute fixes the termination date of an early move-out that is abandonment on the abandonment date, and the 45 days run from it. The landlord's protection is the right to keep the balance, not a later clock.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)

atoms.condition: A chapter 12 provision measures a period in business days.
atoms.effect: A business day is a Monday through Friday that is not a legal holiday under 2.2-3300 (including the Friday or Monday observed when a holiday falls on a weekend, and any day appointed as a holiday by the Governor or the President). construction.quote: a weekday that is not a holiday

the act may be performed or the action may be filed on the next business day that is not a Saturday, Sunday, legal holiday, or day on which the state or local government office is closed
generally does not include Saturdays, Sundays, or legal holidays

atoms.reasoning: Chapter 12 and Title 1 do not define "business day", so the term takes its plain and ordinary meaning from a general-purpose dictionary (the method in Tomlin, quoted in Turner): a weekday that is not a holiday. The Code's own usage agrees: 1-210(E) speaks of the "next business day that is not a Saturday, Sunday, legal holiday", and 2.2-3300 makes each legal holiday a holiday "as to the transaction of all business". The Virginia FOIA Council read the parallel undefined term "working day" the same way (persuasive only). The two Title 59.1 definitions that count Saturdays are confined by their own words to their chapters (health spas and campgrounds); the General Assembly defines a special meaning when it wants one and gave chapter 12 none, so the ordinary meaning governs.

atoms.quote: means the part of a day on which a bank is open to the public for carrying on substantially all of its banking functions, but shall not include Saturday, Sunday or a legal holiday

a weekday that is not a holiday

atoms.reasoning: "Business banking day" joins two terms. "Business day" has its ordinary meaning (VA:business-day-meaning). "Banking day" is defined in the Code's banking title (8.4-104(a)(3)) as a day a bank is open for substantially all of its functions, excluding Saturday, Sunday and legal holidays; a statute about deposits into bank escrow accounts is read in harmony with that definition. A day qualifies only if it is both, which matches the purpose: the deposit is due within five days on which it can actually be banked.

The parties may enter into a written rental agreement at any time during the 12-month tenancy created by this subsection.

every part of a statute is presumed to have some effect and no part will be considered meaningless unless absolutely necessary

Every one of those rules ties a late charge to the rental agreement: 1204(E) requires a written-agreement term, 1226(A)(i) lets the deposit cover late charges "specified in the rental agreement", and 1245(H) lets the landlord recover late charges "contracted for". means a person entitled only under the terms of a rental agreement to occupy a dwelling unit to the exclusion of others and includes a roomer.
shall be itemized by the landlord in a written notice given to the tenant, together with any amount due to the tenant, within 45 days after the termination date of the tenancy

atoms.reasoning: The 55.1-1200 definitions apply "unless the context requires a different meaning". Chapter 12 consistently uses "tenant" for the person whose tenancy has ended wherever a duty runs after termination: the 45-day itemization and refund go "to the tenant" after the termination date (1226(A)), the forwarding address comes from "one of the tenants" (1226(B)), and the two-year deduction records are open to "a tenant" (1226(F)). atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)

atoms.condition: The landlord claims as actual damages rent after the tenancy ended early (abandonment under 55.1-1249, early termination under 55.1-1226(A), a deceased sole tenant under 55.1-1256(C), or other breach).
atoms.effect: The landlord must make reasonable efforts, at reasonable expense, to re-let the unit and so reduce the loss. Rent is recoverable only to the extent reasonable efforts would not have avoided it: rent received from a replacement tenant reduces the claim, the claim ends when a new tenancy begins or the term expires, whichever first, and loss that reasonable efforts would have avoided is not recoverable. The landlord need not incur unreasonable expense. The tenant (or the estate) bears the burden of proving that the landlord failed to mitigate and the amount that reasonable efforts would have saved. Accelerated rent is not recoverable (VA:55.1-1251-no-acceleration).
atoms.quote: Actual damages for breach of the rental agreement may include a claim for rent that would have accrued until the expiration of the term of the rental agreement or until a tenancy pursuant to a new rental agreement commences, whichever occurs first, provided that nothing contained in this section shall diminish the duty of the landlord to mitigate actual damages for breach of the rental agreement.

construction.quote: when one is entitled to the benefit of a contract and can save himself from loss arising from a breach thereof at a trifling expense, or upon reasonable exertion, it is his duty to do it, and he can charge the delinquent party with such damages only as with reasonable endeavor and expense could not be prevented

the seller nonetheless has the duty of making reasonable efforts to mitigate damages resulting from the breach, and to the extent that the seller fails to do so, he may not recover the additional damages incurred
Forbes, as the party asserting this defense, bore the burden of proof on that issue
The General Assembly has taken no steps to abrogate the common-law
post-breach mitigation, including favorable substitute transactions, will reduce the breaching party

atoms.reasoning: At common law a Virginia landlord owed no duty to re-let after abandonment (Crowder, 1920), and that rule still governs nonresidential leases because the General Assembly has not altered it (Bistro Manila, Ct. App. 2025). For residential tenancies chapter 12 alters it: 55.1-1251, 55.1-1249 and 55.1-1256(C) impose a duty to mitigate. The statute names the duty without defining it, so it carries the content of Virginia's general mitigation rule, which Crowder states (reasonable exertion and expense; only unavoidable loss is chargeable) and which the Supreme Court of Virginia applies to real-estate contracts in Forbes v. Rapp (2005): reasonable efforts, no recovery of damages that reasonable efforts would have avoided, and the burden of proof on the breaching party asserting the defense. Dominion v. Alstom (2019) confirms that substitute transactions after a breach reduce contract damages, so replacement rent reduces the claim.

Paying the refund to the contact does not discharge the landlord against the personal representative or the successors. The refund is paid to the personal representative, or to a successor under 64.2-601 or 64.2-602, and that payment discharges the landlord (64.2-603).

Any person to whom payment or delivery of a small asset has been made is answerable and accountable therefor to any personal representative of the decedent's estate

atoms.reasoning: 55.1-1256 is about the property left in the unit: (A) lets the landlord dispose of "the personal property left in the dwelling unit or upon the premises", and (B)'s right to "claim the personal property" refers to that same property; the words that follow, "otherwise handle the affairs of the deceased tenant with the landlord", confer authority to deal with the landlord, not title to the estate's money. The General Assembly wrote a discharge in Title 64.2 and none in 55.1-1256(B); a discharge is not implied where the specific statute on paying a decedent's assets supplies one only for named payees. The authorized contact becomes the payee only by also being the personal representative or a qualifying successor.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)

atoms.condition: At move-out the landlord deducts from the deposit, or claims, for the condition of the unit.
atoms.effect: Reasonable wear and tear is the deterioration that results from the tenant's ordinary, reasonable use of the unit and its fixtures over the time of occupancy (normal depreciation from use and age). It is not chargeable. Chargeable damage is loss caused by the tenant's breach of 55.1-1227: deliberate or negligent destruction, defacement, damage, impairment or removal by the tenant or anyone the tenant permits, unreasonable use of fixtures and appliances, or failure to keep the unit clean. The baseline is the move-in report, deemed correct unless objected to (55.1-1214). Where an item was both worn and damaged, the charge is the cost of the damage less a reasonable allowance for the wear the item had already undergone (its depreciation), not the cost of a new item.
atoms.quote: the payment of the amount of damages that the landlord has suffered by reason of the tenant's noncompliance with § 55.1-1227, less reasonable wear and tear

construction.quote: the loss, injury, or stress to which something is subjected by or in the course of use
normal depreciation
Use in a reasonable manner all utilities and all electrical, plumbing, sanitary, heating, ventilating, air-conditioning, and other facilities and appliances
Not deliberately or negligently destroy, deface, damage, impair, or remove any part of the premises or permit any person, whether known by the tenant or not, to do so
deduct from such cost a reasonable allowance for the wear and tear thereof since its erection

itemizing damages to the dwelling unit existing at the time of occupancy, and the report shall be deemed correct unless the tenant objects to it in writing within five days after receipt of the report

atoms.reasoning: Chapter 12 does not define the phrase, so it takes its ordinary meaning: loss from the course of use, especially normal depreciation (general-purpose dictionary, the method Virginia courts use). The statute's structure fixes the line: 55.1-1226(A)(ii) allows deductions only for damage from the tenant's noncompliance with 55.1-1227, less reasonable wear and tear, and 1227 defines noncompliance as unreasonable use of facilities and deliberate or negligent damage. Deterioration from reasonable use is therefore wear and tear. The Supreme Court of Virginia treats reasonable wear and tear as an allowance for depreciation deducted from cost (Newton v. White, 1914), which gives the measure where an item was both worn and damaged. The move-in report fixes the starting condition. Whether a given use was reasonable and how far an item had worn are judgments the operator makes on the evidence.
