A landlord and tenant may include in a rental agreement terms and conditions not prohibited by this chapter or other rule of law

atoms.reasoning: Under Windmill Meadows (2014) a new statute governs obligations under an existing agreement that are not yet due on its effective date when its context shows that intent; no set form of words is required. 1245(G) shows it on its face: it measures the plan amount by late charges "contracted for in the rental agreement" and then bars "additional" late fees on that amount, so it is written to operate on the late-fee terms leases already contain. It takes nothing accrued: late charges already incurred on the missed rent stay in the amount due (1-239 preserves accrued rights), and the bar reaches only fees that would arise after the effective date, during a plan that can be offered only for rent unpaid on or after 2027-07-01. Lease terms have always been valid only if "not prohibited by this chapter" (1204(A)).

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.provision: 55.1-1200 "damage insurance", 55.1-1206(A), 55.1-1226(E) seventh sentence: recovery after the provider pays
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.condition: The tenant's damage insurance (bond or commercial insurance under 55.1-1200 and 55.1-1226(I)) paid the landlord's claim for a loss the tenant caused.
atoms.effect: The landlord may recover from the tenant only the part of the loss the payment did not cover (e.g. amounts above the coverage limit, a deductible, or items the provider denied), together with other recoverable charges under 55.1-1245(H). The landlord may not recover from the tenant the amount the provider paid.
atoms.quote: A plaintiff is not allowed to recover for a breach of contract more than the actual loss sustained by him

construction.quote: requires a case-specific determination of whether the parties
to secure the performance by the tenant of the terms and conditions of the rental agreement and to replace all or part of a security deposit
such payments shall not be deemed a security deposit, but shall be rent

atoms.reasoning: Contract damages compensate actual loss and no more (Orebaugh, as restated in Dominion v. Alstom, 2019). Dominion allows the collateral-source exception in contract cases only where the parties' expectations support it, chiefly where the injured party itself paid for the collateral benefit. Here the opposite holds: the tenant pays the premiums as rent (55.1-1206(A)), and the coverage exists by definition to secure the tenant's performance and replace a security deposit (55.1-1200). The parties' expectation is that a payment under it satisfies the tenant's obligation to the landlord to that extent, as an applied deposit would. A second recovery of the same loss from the tenant would put the landlord in a better position than performance, which Virginia contract law forbids.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.provision: 55.1-1206(A): damage insurance the landlord obtains on the tenant's behalf
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.condition: The landlord obtained the damage insurance on the tenant's behalf (the policy must cover the tenant as an insured, and the tenant bears its cost), and the insurer paid the landlord for a covered loss the tenant caused.
atoms.effect: Neither the landlord nor the insurer as the landlord's subrogee may recover that covered loss from the tenant, even if the tenant's negligence caused it. Loss outside the coverage remains recoverable from the tenant (VA:damage-insurance-landlord-recovery).
atoms.quote: Where a landlord obtains damage insurance coverage on behalf of a tenant, the insurance policy shall provide coverage for the tenant as an insured.

construction.quote: may not recover for that loss from the defendant even if the loss is caused by the defendant

atoms.reasoning: The Supreme Court of Virginia holds that where the plaintiff has undertaken to protect the defendant from a loss by procuring insurance, neither the plaintiff nor its subrogee may recover that loss from the defendant (Walker v. Vanderpool, 1983). A landlord that obtains damage insurance for its tenant must, by statute, make the tenant an insured, and charges the tenant the cost, so the landlord has undertaken exactly that protection. The Walker rule therefore bars both the landlord and the insurer standing in its shoes from recovering the covered loss from the tenant.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 49, Chapter 3 (relief of sureties)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.condition: The damage insurance is a bond on which the provider is surety for the tenant's performance, and the surety paid the landlord's claim in whole or in part.
atoms.effect: The surety may obtain judgment against the tenant for the amount paid, with interest from payment and five percent damages, and is substituted by operation of law to the landlord's rights for that amount. The landlord keeps its rights against the tenant for any unpaid balance, and does not itself collect the paid amount again (VA:damage-insurance-landlord-recovery).
atoms.quote: shall, by operation of law, in addition to the remedy above provided, be substituted to and become the owner of all of the rights and remedies of the creditor for the enforcement and collection of the amount or amounts so paid

construction.quote: obtain a judgment or decree against any person against whom such right of action exists for the amount so paid, with interest from the time of payment, and five per centum damages on such amount

atoms.reasoning: 55.1-1200 defines damage insurance to include "a bond" securing the tenant's performance; a provider on such a bond is a surety and the tenant its principal. 49-27 gives a paying surety judgment against the principal and subrogation to the creditor's rights, while preserving the creditor's rights to any balance. It applies by its terms to any surety on a bond.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.provision: 55.1-1206(A) separate policy / 55.1-1226(I) insurance obtained by the tenant
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.condition: The tenant obtained its own commercial damage insurance policy (a separate policy under 55.1-1206(A), or coverage in lieu of a deposit under 55.1-1226(I)) and the insurer paid the landlord.
atoms.effect: The insurer's right to recover the payment from the tenant is fixed by the policy's subrogation or reimbursement terms (EXT:VA-damage-insurance-policy); no Virginia statute addresses it, and Virginia applies no general rule barring an insurer's recovery against a person the policy names as an insured. Whatever the policy provides, the landlord recovers from the tenant only the uncovered part of the loss (VA:damage-insurance-landlord-recovery).
atoms.quote: Federal relies upon a rule sometimes applied in other jurisdictions

construction.quote: requires a case-specific determination of whether the parties

atoms.reasoning: Chapter 12 regulates the coverage only through the 1226(I) criteria and says nothing about the insurer's rights against the tenant. In Federal Insurance v. Starr Electric (1991) the Supreme Court of Virginia described the no-subrogation-against-an-insured rule as one applied in other jurisdictions and decided the case on the policy and the parties' agreement, so in Virginia the policy's terms decide the insurer's recourse. The Walker rule (VA:damage-insurance-landlord-procured) does not reach a policy the tenant bought for itself, because the landlord undertook no duty to insure the tenant. The landlord's own recovery is limited in every case by the actual-loss rule.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.condition: More than one tenant is on the rental agreement and one of them moves out while the tenancy continues for the others.
atoms.effect: No deposit disposition is due: the deposit is applied and itemized only on termination of the tenancy (or vacating, whichever occurs last), and the tenancy has not terminated. The departing person remains a tenant on the rental agreement, with its obligations, unless the agreement is changed with written consent (55.1-1204(I)). Co-tenants remain responsible for the rent for the rest of the term.
atoms.quote: Upon termination of the tenancy or the date the tenant vacates the dwelling unit, whichever occurs last

construction.quote: No unilateral change in the terms of a rental agreement by a landlord or tenant shall be valid unless (i) notice of the change is given in accordance with the terms of the rental agreement or as otherwise required by law and (ii) both parties consent in writing to the change.

atoms.reasoning: 55.1-1226(A) ties application and itemization of the deposit to termination of the tenancy; one co-tenant's departure does not terminate a tenancy that continues for the others. A person stops being a party to the rental agreement only by a change the parties consent to in writing (1204(I)); 1236(E) confirms that co-tenants who stay remain liable for the rent.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.provision: 55.1-1226(B) "unless otherwise agreed to in writing by each of the tenants"; 18VAC135-20-181(B)(2)(d)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.condition: More than one tenant is on the rental agreement and the landlord is asked to refund part of the deposit to a departing co-tenant, or to substitute a new co-tenant's deposit, before the tenancy ends.
atoms.effect: Lawful only on the written agreement of each tenant. Without it, the deposit stays for disposition at termination by one check payable to all tenants, and a payment to one tenant does not reduce the landlord's duty to account to all tenants for the whole deposit. With it, the refund or substitution follows the agreement and the remaining deposit continues under 55.1-1226. A licensee may disburse escrowed deposit funds only as the lease, the management agreement or statute provides, so the written agreement must exist before the disbursement. Where a new party takes over by assignment or sublease, the landlord may hold a deposit from only one party (55.1-1226(H)).
atoms.quote: Where there is more than one tenant subject to a rental agreement, unless otherwise agreed to in writing by each of the tenants, disposition of the security deposit shall be made with one check being payable to all such tenants and sent to a forwarding address provided by one of the tenants.

construction.quote: Escrow funds must remain in an escrow account until disbursed in accordance with the terms of the lease, the property management agreement, or the applicable statutory provisions.
If the tenant has any assignee or sublessee, the landlord shall be entitled to hold a security deposit from only one party

atoms.reasoning: 55.1-1226(B) makes the deposit disposable only to all tenants together unless each tenant agrees otherwise in writing, so a partial refund to one tenant is a departure from that rule that each tenant must approve in writing. Chapter 12 has no other mechanism for a partial disposition during a continuing tenancy. The Real Estate Board regulation independently limits a licensee's disbursements to those the lease, the management agreement or statute authorizes.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.condition: One tenant is on the rental agreement and an amount is due to the tenant at disposition.
atoms.effect: Chapter 12 prescribes no payment instrument for a single tenant: the landlord may pay by check, money order or electronic transfer to the tenant, so long as the amount due goes to the tenant with the written itemization within the 45-day period. A tenant's electronic payment of the deposit creates no duty to refund electronically.
atoms.quote: shall be itemized by the landlord in a written notice given to the tenant, together with any amount due to the tenant, within 45 days after the termination date of the tenancy

construction.quote: Where there is more than one tenant subject to a rental agreement, unless otherwise agreed to in writing by each of the tenants, disposition of the security deposit shall be made with one check being payable to all such tenants and sent to a forwarding address provided by one of the tenants.

atoms.reasoning: 55.1-1226(A) requires the amount due to accompany the itemization and says nothing about the instrument. The only instrument rule, one check, is expressly conditioned on there being more than one tenant (1226(B)). Where the General Assembly confines a rule to one case, it does not extend to others, so a single tenant may be paid by any method that delivers the amount due.

atoms.instrument: Code of Virginia, Title 55.1, Chapter 12 (Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.condition: More than one tenant is on the rental agreement.
atoms.effect: Without a written agreement of each tenant: one check payable to all tenants, sent to a forwarding address provided by one of them; separate checks, split amounts or electronic payment are not a compliant disposition. With a written agreement of each tenant: the disposition follows that agreement (e.g. separate refunds in agreed shares, or electronic transfer to each). With no forwarding address: the written disposition is still due within 45 days, the refund may be held in escrow, and after one more year may be remitted to the State Treasurer (VA:55.1-1226(B)-no-forwarding, VA:55.1-1226(B)-unclaimed).
atoms.quote: Where there is more than one tenant subject to a rental agreement, unless otherwise agreed to in writing by each of the tenants, disposition of the security deposit shall be made with one check being payable to all such tenants and sent to a forwarding address provided by one of the tenants.

early_termination.note: A written early-termination agreement fixes the date (1253(A)). An early move-out that is abandonment (keys returned) terminates the agreement that day and starts the 45 days; if abandonment is established only by the 1249 notice, termination falls on the seventh day after it. The landlord gives the disposition within 45 days and keeps any balance against 1251 damages, which are limited by reasonable mitigation efforts (burden on the tenant).

damage_above_deposit_needing_contractor.note: Written contractor notice within 45 days buys 15 more days for the itemization and repair cost. Charges exclude reasonable wear and tear (deterioration from reasonable use; worn items are charged net of depreciation). The excess over the deposit is recoverable as damages, with or without suit. Only intentional noncompliance triggers the 1226(E) remedy.

utility_withholding.note: 1226(C) withholding covers only the tenant's obligation to a third-party provider, and only after the required advance notice. Utilities the landlord bills itself (submetering, RUBS, local fees) are rent or lease charges applied under 1226(A)(i)/(iii), not withholding. A deadline ending on a weekend or holiday rolls to the next business day (1-210(E)).

damage_insurance_instead_of_deposit.note: No deposit exists to apply. Unpaid premiums are rent. After the provider pays, the landlord recovers from the tenant only the uncovered loss; a bond surety may recover from the tenant under 49-27; a landlord-procured policy bars recovery of the covered loss from the tenant (Walker); a tenant's own policy governs the insurer's recourse.

multiple_tenants_one_leaving.note: No disposition is due while the tenancy continues for the others. A partial refund or substitution needs each tenant's written agreement; at termination, one check payable to all unless each tenant agrees otherwise in writing.

no_forwarding_address.note: Serve the disposition at the last known residence (may be the unit) within 45 days, hold any refund in escrow, and remit to the State Treasurer after one more year if the landlord chooses. Remitting ends the landlord's liability.

building_sold_mid_tenancy.note: Whoever holds the landlord's interest at termination owes the deposit, whether or not it was transferred. The seller is relieved for later events after a good-faith sale and notice.

abandoned_property.note: Sale proceeds go first to the tenant's debt and reasonable costs; any remainder is treated as a security deposit and joins the 1226 disposition.

statement_due_on_weekend_or_holiday.note: The event day is excluded. A last day on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday may roll to the next business day. "Gives" is met by sending, so the send date is what counts.

licensee_manager_holding_deposit_in_escr.note: Deposit in escrow within 5 business banking days; disburse only under the lease, the management agreement or 1226, and only against sufficient funds for that client. Keep records 3 years (REB) and deduction records 2 years (1226(F)).

balance_pursued_handed_off_or_written_of.note: Extra walk (not in the STAGE_A.md list) for the last link of the chain.

not_arising_in_virginia: NYC rent-stabilized, rent-controlled, 6+ unit and under-6 unit cases; pre/post-2019 HSTPA leases (New York only). The Virginia analogue for version timing is UNK:VA-2027-versions-existing-leases and VA:Acts2014-c651-cl4 for pre-2015 deposit interest.

deceased_sole_tenant.note: Tenancy deemed terminated on the date of death (1256(C)), so the 45-day clock runs from the later of that date and vacating. Give the itemization to the authorized contact; pay the refund only to a personal representative or a 64.2-601/602 successor (discharge under 64.2-603), holding it until one exists.

lease_signed_before_2027_amendments.note: Amendments are prospective (1-238) and govern acts and events on or after their effective dates, whatever the lease date; accrued rights stay under the old text (1-239). The 1245(G) late-fee bar applies to plans for rent unpaid on or after 2027-07-01 even where the lease provides late fees; late charges accrued before the plan remain collectible through it.
